title.en: Adar transformed; Purim misunderstood

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the whole month of Adar was turned to joy, and that Purim is misunderstood as a kind of Jewish Halloween when it may be the greatest day of the year. Its clowning and wine are like an anesthetic for a remedy too strong to take awake.

title.en: A whole masechta for a small Yom Tov

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Purim, a weekday Yom Tov with few halachos, earned its own masechta, unlike Chanukah or Shavuos. The Gemara explains the whole Megillah and opens it with about fifteen Sages, each bringing a passuk as a key to it.

title.en: Rav Masna's key: Hashem is near

summary.en: Rav Masna opens the Megillah with the passuk about a great nation to whom Hashem is near; the Mashgiach explains that the events of the Megillah could have made Jews think Hashem was far, and the Megillah teaches the opposite. He then asks why Rashi, usually so terse, poetically calls the Megillah 'the letter of Purim'.

title.en: A book and a letter

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts a book, written for whoever picks it up, with a letter, addressed privately to one person and read with closer attention. The Megillah is both, and its message is meant personally for every reader, even one who thinks Hashem's blessings are for others.

title.en: The ladder of souls and generations

summary.en: Recalling the three dimensions of creation, space, time and soul, the Mashgiach describes souls arranged on a ladder in each generation and across history, from the Avos and the dor hamidbar at the head down to our generation, 'ikvesa d'Meshicha', the insensitive heel.

title.en: The embryo, the fingernail and Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the heel is no less part of the person: in the embryo every limb, even the last-formed fingernail, was included. So the last generation is still bound to the beginning, just as every place in the world is nourished from Yerushalayim, as shown by Shlomo HaMelech's planting.

title.en: Nisan the flag, Adar the cloak

summary.en: In time, Nisan, when the world was created, is the head of the months; its name comes from 'nes', a flag on a high pole, because Hashem shows Himself openly with miracles then. Adar, furthest away, comes from 'aderes', a cloak, the time when a person is in the dark and Hashem hides.

title.en: Hidden miracles: uncovering the hidden

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the supernatural miracles of Yetzias Mitzrayim with the Megillah, where every event is natural and could appear in a newspaper. Yet taken together the plot shows a guiding hand, so the Megillah is full of miracles; following the Avodas Yisrael, 'Megillas Esther' means revealing the hidden, recognizing Hashem behind the mask.

title.en: Dan at the rear and Amalek

summary.en: Adar draws from Nisan as the toe from the head. The Mashgiach describes Dan, the tribe at the rear of the camp, gathering what others lost, and its failings; Amalek attacked those expelled from the clouds, thinking Hashem had rejected them. Adar, like Dan, is at the bottom, and Parshas Zachor teaches that Hashem never forsakes any Jewish soul.

title.en: The Megillah's hope for the last generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the Jews joined Achashverosh's feast, celebrating the apparent end of the seventy years, and lost hope; that generation at the end of the first galus corresponds to ours. The Megillah's personal letter tells every Jew that Hashem is near and has not forsaken him, and it ends with the Jews' teshuvah and with gentiles becoming Jews.

title.en: A second Adar: the moon falls behind

summary.en: The Mashgiach leaves the halachos of drinking for later weeks and turns to this year's second Adar. Hashem is the sun and Jews the moon, so they count by the moon; when the moon lags, a thirteenth month is added, taking the Jews even further from Nisan. The Yerushalmi says the original Purim miracle happened in Adar Sheni.

title.en: The thirteenth month and the kolel

summary.en: The twelve months and twelve tribes match the twelve permutations of the Divine Name; the thirteenth month, like outcasts belonging to no tribe, has none, and is counted as the 'kolel', the added one. The Mashgiach asks where the right to add one comes from and answers that the One is Hashem, as in the Midrash that Hashem completed the seventy souls and the six hundred thousand.

title.en: Purim Gadol: the Yom Tov of the lowest

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that in a leap year the second Purim is a 'great Purim', when Hashem joins those left out and completes Klal Yisrael, so no Jew is rejected. Unlike Shabbos, felt most by tzaddikim, Purim is made for the lowest, and the lower one is, the more Purim can lift him.

catalogTitle: הכנת עני לשבועות - שועתנו קבל ושמע צעקתנו

oneLiner.en: On the last day of sefirah the Mashgiach teaches that the true preparation for Shavuos is the cry of "shavaseinu kabel" from one who knows he is not ready, the power of tefillah shown in Megillas Ruth, and serving Hashem with freshness and seriousness.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach notes that Shavuos, unlike Pesach and Sukkos, has no physical preparation; its preparation is kedushah, unity and teshuvah, worked on through the days of sefirah. One who reaches the last week and sees how little he has achieved has the line of Ana Bekoach for that week: "shavaseinu kabel... yodea ta'alumos", a cry to Hashem who knows the hidden wish of every Jew to accept the Torah. Even the hagbalah at Sinai, knowing one may not go up, is itself a preparation. He then explains why Megillas Ruth is read on Shavuos: the Targum lists ten famines, the last a hunger to hear the word of Hashem before Moshiach, and Boaz ended his famine through tefillah; the megillah, the lineage of Dovid, the pillar of tefillah, comes to teach the power of prayer. He goes on to demand freshness and seriousness in avodah: Ruth against Orpah, Tosafos on kalus rosh at Matan Torah, no idle talk before davening, and davening with the tzibbur, and closes with a call to cry out on the last day of sefirah.

en: Shavuos has no physical preparation; its preparation is drawing kedushah onto oneself, unity among Jews and teshuvah, through the days of sefirah.

The line of Ana Bekoach for the last week of sefirah, "shavaseinu kabel... yodea ta'alumos", is the cry of one who is not prepared, relying on Hashem who knows the hidden wish of every Jew to accept the Torah.

Megillas Ruth is read on Shavuos to teach the power of tefillah: Boaz ended the famine through prayer, and the last famine, the hunger for the word of Hashem before Moshiach, will also be broken only by tefillah.
Avodas Hashem must stay fresh and not grow old or sleepy; the success of one's service depends on that freshness.
Seriousness is essential in avodah; lightheadedness (kalus rosh) is a great obstacle, and according to Tosafos it is what the Torah guarded against before Matan Torah.
Idle talk before davening ruins the whole tefillah, and coldness in one person spreads to others.

title.en: Preparing for Shavuos without an act

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Shavuos with Pesach and Sukkos, which require physical preparation, and explains that its preparation is kedushah, unity and teshuvah through sefirah. For one who reaches the last week unprepared he brings the line of Ana Bekoach, "shavaseinu kabel... yodea ta'alumos", a cry to Hashem who knows the hidden wish to accept the Torah.

title.en: The hagbalah and the last cry of sefirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the three days of hagbalah, being held back from going up Har Sinai, teach a person to know he is not ready, and that this itself prepares him for the gift of Torah. The last week of sefirah is one great cry to Hashem, and its verse, "afsei aretz", shows that one reaches the lowest point and from there receives the Torah.

title.en: Coming to Shavuos like a convert

summary.en: From the middle branch of the menorah psalm the Mashgiach teaches that on Shavuos one should see himself as a goy about to convert, like Ruth, immersing at dawn for the sake of geirus. Shavuos is a mikveh, and the two loaves are Torah and tefillah, which depend on each other.

title.en: The fifth of Sivan, a day of tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls the last day of sefirah, the fifth of Sivan when Jews said na'aseh v'nishma, a day of tefillah and kabbalas ol, a day to daven for one's share in Torah for the whole year. He explains that this is why Ruth, from whom Dovid the pillar of tefillah descends, is read on Shavuos.

title.en: The ten famines and the Targum on Ruth

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the opening of Megillas Ruth with the Targum's list of ten famines, the last of them a hunger to hear the word of Hashem before Moshiach, which he says we are living through. He shows that the Targum says twice that Boaz ended the famine through prayer, and asks why it repeats this and why the megillah mentions all ten famines.

title.en: Ruth teaches the power of tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that Megillas Ruth, the lineage of Dovid the pillar of tefillah, comes to teach the power of prayer: the tenth and strongest famine will be stilled only by tefillah. The megillah is a psak written by Shmuel, and a psak restates its reason at the end, so the Targum repeats Boaz's prayer.

title.en: Staying warm and fresh in avodah

summary.en: After asking the listeners to daven for a sick friend, the Mashgiach speaks of unity and of warming one another, since what is not kept warm grows cold. He brings that all of Moshe Rabbeinu's ascents came through rising early, that a kos shel brachah must be fresh, and that the chevra was founded on warm davening, and demands that every day be like new.

title.en: Ruth and Orpah: freshness and seriousness

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares Ruth and Orpah: both accepted the yoke of Heaven, but only Ruth's acceptance stayed fresh and lasting, and from her came Dovid while from Orpah came Golias. He then demands seriousness against lightheadedness, entering shul with joy and not talking during davening.

title.en: Tosafos: kalus rosh at Matan Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Shabbos on the three days of separation before Matan Torah, and Tosafos' question why a ba'al keri could not receive the Torah before there was any tumah. Following Tosafos' second answer, he explains that the concern was kalus rosh, since Torah must be received with awe and trembling.

title.en: Coffee and talk before davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach says coffee before davening is for strength, not for settling down to chat and joke, and that talk before davening ruins the tefillah. He tells of a tzaddik who shared his bread in a concentration camp and from whose way of drinking coffee one could learn yiras shamayim, and brings the Gemara's reasoning that some could not have been immersing while others were receiving the Torah.

title.en: Davening with toil and with the tzibbur

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the hanhagos printed at the end of Noam Elimelech, not to speak before davening, and says the Ba'al Shem Tov re-established the pillar of tefillah. He describes how Ahavah Rabbah once took two hours, brings Rashi that a blessing must not be said in haste but with a full heart, and warns of the danger of davening alone rather than with the tzibbur.

title.en: Shavuos night and the final cry

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains, with the Zohar and Midrash Tanchuma, that Shavuos is a mikveh and that staying up all night with toil in Torah shows willing acceptance of the Oral Torah that was once accepted under compulsion. He returns to "shavaseinu kabel" as the last cry of sefirah, brings the Kozhnitzer Maggid that the last day can make up all fifty, and closes with brachos.

catalogTitle: מקבלים תורה מחדש; נחיצות הכנה לשבועות; לא לעשות מעיקר טפל ומטפל עיקר; לשפוך נפשו באהבה רבה

oneLiner.en: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan the Mashgiach teaches that Matan Torah truly returns every year, that Shavuos is named for its preparation, and that one must not let the night's vigil ruin the morning's davening and Krias HaTorah, the heart of receiving the Torah.

abstract.en: Opening with Rashi on the Jews' arrival at Sinai on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, the Mashgiach explains that every Yom Tov repeats itself each year, comparing the year to a rotating card file where each day's card comes round again. Matan Torah therefore happens every year: tzaddikim like the Belzer Rav see it, and even coarse people's souls receive it, as a numbed tooth is worked on without feeling. Because the Yom Tov is named Shavuos after the weeks of preparation, the Mashgiach stresses teshuvah on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, unity, the special Shavuos mikveh and a heartfelt Ahavah Rabbah. He warns against making the main thing secondary: staying up all night and then sleeping through davening, Krias HaTorah and the Kedushah of Musaf, like a chassan who spent on everything but forgot the ring. He closes with the rare reading of Naso before Shavuos and a prayer for salvation.

en: Every Yom Tov repeats itself each year, like a card on a rotating wheel that comes round again, so Matan Torah truly happens every Shavuos.
Great tzaddikim perceive Matan Torah as it was at Sinai; others feel it according to their level, and even those who feel nothing still receive it in their soul.
The Yom Tov is called Shavuos, after the weeks of preparation, because the preparation is so central that it gives the Yom Tov its name.
The preparation includes teshuvah from Rosh Chodesh Sivan, unity among Jews, and the special mikveh of Shavuos morning.
Staying awake all night must not come at the cost of davening, Krias HaTorah and the Kedushah of Musaf, which are the main thing of Shavuos.
A Jew's success in learning all year comes from Shavuos, and Ahavah Rabbah on Shavuos should be said with an outpouring of the heart.

candidateTopics: Shavuos night vigil and morning davening

title.en: Each Yom Tov comes round again

summary.en: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan the Mashgiach brings Rashi that the arrival at Sinai was in teshuvah, then explains that every Yom Tov repeats itself yearly, comparing the year to a rotating card file. Therefore Matan Torah happens every year.

title.en: Seeing Matan Torah: the Shinever Rav

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Shinever Rav wanted to travel to Belz to experience Matan Torah, and his father the Sanzer Rav showed it to him at home. He explains that each Jew experiences Matan Torah by his level, likening those who feel nothing to a numbed tooth, and that all of Sefirah prepares for the reading of the Aseres HaDibros.

title.en: A Yom Tov named for its preparation

summary.en: The Mashgiach says no mitzvah is prepared for like Shavuos, and that the Yom Tov is named for the weeks of preparation rather than for the Torah. He calls for teshuvah from Rosh Chodesh Sivan, as Rashi teaches, and for the unity of 'one heart' that preceded Matan Torah.

title.en: The Shavuos mikveh and Ahavah Rabbah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a mikveh, like a sukkah, is holy through the holy names that the halachos bring into it, and that the mikveh of Shavuos morning is a different kind of mikveh. He adds that Pesukei Dezimra and Ahavah Rabbah of Shavuos are part of the preparation, recalling how long Ahavah Rabbah took in Tsanz.

title.en: The vigil and the forgotten ring

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns against staying up all night and then dozing through davening and the Kedushah of Musaf, where the great union takes place, citing the Ropshitzer, the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Minchas Elazar. He compares it to a chassan who paid for everything at the wedding but forgot the ring.

title.en: The Ahavas Yisroel and the main thing

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Ahavas Yisroel of Vizhnitz sent a group of yeshiva students to sleep so that they could daven properly, and says that one who knows a short rest will not suffice should not stay up Shavuos night. He mentions the Imrei Emes's takanah to daven early and repeats: do not make the main thing secondary.

title.en: Shavuos as a day of judgment; tears at Ahavah Rabbah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that one should fear Shavuos more than Rosh Hashanah, since then one is judged on Torah and mitzvos, and a bochur's success in learning all year comes from it. He calls for Ahavah Rabbah with tears, and returns to teshuvah on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, which contains the whole of Shavuos.

title.en: Parshas Naso before Shavuos; a prayer for salvation

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that this year Parshas Naso is read before Shavuos, which almost never happens, and suggests it may be so that the merit of the twelve nesi'im should nullify the twelve princes of Yishmael at a time of danger. He ties Shavuos to Moshiach through Dovid HaMelech and the Ba'al Shem Tov, and closes with a call to use the coming days and a blessing to receive the Torah with joy.

catalogTitle: אנכי ה' - האמונה למעלה מן השכל בחורים צעירים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the fiftieth day, on which the Torah and 'Anochi Hashem' were given, is above time, number and intellect, and that the emunah received there is what a Jew in the last generation must hold on to, driving out every thought of doubt.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with three questions about Shavuos: we count only forty-nine days, Moshe added a day of his own, and we say 'the time of the giving of our Torah' on a day it was not given. He answers that the fiftieth day is above number and above this world, like the place of the aron that took up no space, and like the Torah, whose pesukim do not fit a count. 'Anochi Hashem' was given above intellect, and that is emunah, which is higher than knowledge. He brings the Ohr HaChaim that before Moshiach Jews will fall into the fiftieth gate of impurity, which is apikorsus, and says the task of this generation is simple faith. He speaks openly to bachurim troubled by doubts: the pain shows they believe, and driving such a thought out fulfills the mitzvah of 'velo sasuru'. With the parable of a building's main switch he shows how much each mitzvah and each sin does above.

en: The fiftieth day is above number and above the seven-day order of the world, so it cannot be counted, and by Heaven's reckoning the day Moshe chose is still the fiftieth.
'Anochi Hashem Elokecha' was given above intellect, time and place, and so it is received as emunah, which is higher than knowledge.
Before Moshiach Jews are pulled into the fiftieth gate of impurity, which is apikorsus, and the task of this generation is to hold on to simple faith in Hashem and in the whole Torah.
Doubts that torment a person are not real doubts but a confusion of the mind, and his pain is itself a sign that he believes.
Even the greatest tzaddik has a moment of doubt, so that he can fulfill the mitzvah of 'velo sasuru' by driving the thought out.
A person does not know his own power: each of his limbs is a switch, and a mitzvah lights up all the worlds while a sin brings destruction.

title.en: Three questions on the fiftieth day

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the count is called fifty but only forty-nine days are counted, how Moshe could add a day, and why the first day of Shavuos is called the time of the giving of the Torah, especially in Eretz Yisrael. He begins to answer that the fiftieth day is above number, which belongs only to this world.

title.en: Above the world, above time and place

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the world was made in seven days and the eighth week and fiftieth day are above it, so by Heaven's reckoning the day Moshe chose is the fiftieth. He compares it to the Kodesh HaKodashim, where the aron took up no space.

title.en: Anochi Hashem: emunah above knowledge

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the Masorah's count of pesukim in parshas Yisro does not fit, because the Torah is above time and number. 'Anochi Hashem' was given above intellect, the redemption was completed on the fiftieth day, and that is why it is received as emunah, which is higher than knowledge.

title.en: The fiftieth gate and simple faith

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ohr HaChaim that before Moshiach Jews will fall into the fiftieth gate of impurity, which he identifies as apikorsus, spread today as never before. The task of the generation is simple faith in Hashem and in the whole Torah, its sages and their chiddushim, which those who learn lishmah see come with heavenly help.

title.en: Bachurim troubled by doubts

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of bachurim and older people who come to him troubled by doubts in emunah, and explains why he speaks about it: such doubts can befall anyone, often through pegamim. He says their pain shows that they believe, and that these are not real doubts but a confusion of the mind, like a person who keeps going back to check that the door is locked.

title.en: Driving out the thought: velo sasuru

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that every Jew, even the greatest tzaddik, has a moment of doubt, so that he can fulfill the mitzvah of 'velo sasuru acharei levavchem'. Bringing the Bnei Yissaschar and the Tanya, he explains that one should not feel bad when such a thought comes, since it comes from the yetzer hara, and driving it out is one of the greatest mitzvos, especially now when the fiftieth gate must be broken.

title.en: The main switch: a person's hidden power

summary.en: The Mashgiach says no person knows how important he is: his 248 limbs and 365 sinews are like buttons, as one push of the main switch lights the whole Empire State Building. A mitzvah lights up all the worlds and a sin like eating treif sets off destruction; he brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that a person must be told his strength, and the elephant that fears a fly.

title.en: Heavenly lamps and the week of malchus

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew who drives out a thought of doubt can save thousands of Jews, and brings the Maggid's reading that everything above comes from you. He describes each Jew's 248 heavenly lamps, brighter the greater he is, mentions Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl who passed away in the week of malchus, and closes with a brachah to receive the Torah with joy, love and fear of Hashem.

catalogTitle: The נסים in Current Events

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that in the last generation, like in the month of Adar, Hashem hides Himself and works His nissim within nature, and the Megillah teaches how to find His hand in the events of our own day.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the structure of 248 limbs, from the skull to the heel, found in man, in the Torah's 248 positive mitzvos, in history and in geography. The first generation, of the Exodus and Matan Torah, is the head; the last generation, ikvesa d'Meshicha, is the heel, the darkest part of the body, and he is convinced it is ours. The calendar too runs from Nisan, the month of revealed nissim, down to Adar, whose name means a cloak. Haman rejoiced when his lot fell in Adar, and especially in Adar Sheni, an appendage like the last eight pesukim of the Torah, written in tears. He did not know that history moves in a circle: after Adar comes Nisan, and the last generation becomes the head. The Megillah has no open nissim and not even Hashem's name; its nissim are hidden in nature, as the Bnei Yissaschar's parable and the chain of Purim events show. Reading the Megillah this way, the Mashgiach says, one can read today's news and see Hashem pulling the strings.

en: The structure of 248 limbs, from head to heel, appears in man, in the mitzvos, in history and in geography.
The first generation, which saw the Exodus and Matan Torah, is the head; the last generation, ikvesa d'Meshicha, is the heel, and the Mashgiach is convinced it is ours.
Nisan is the month of revealed nissim, while Adar, meaning a cloak, is the month in which Hashem conceals Himself.
Haman's mistake was to see history as a straight line; it is a circle, and after Adar comes Nisan.
The Megillah has no supernatural nissim and does not mention Hashem's name; its nissim are hidden within nature.
The Megillah is an exercise in finding Hashem between the words, and one who reads it correctly can see Him conducting today's events too.

title.en: From head to heel: man, history, geography

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the structure of 248 limbs, from the skull to the heel, in man, in the 248 positive mitzvos, in the generations and in the places of the world. The first generation is the head and ours, the heel of Moshiach, is the last, but since the line is a circle the last generation will become the head again.

title.en: Nisan and Adar: revelation and concealment

summary.en: The calendar runs from Nisan, when the first generation saw Hashem's nissim, down to Adar, whose name means a cloak. Haman rejoiced when his lot fell in Adar, thinking Hashem makes no nissim then; the Mashgiach brings the Gemara's source for Esther in the Torah, Hashem hiding His face, and the Yerushalmi that the Purim miracle happened in Adar Sheni.

title.en: Appendages: the Torah's last letters and Adar Sheni

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Torah's 600,000 letters correspond to 600,000 Jewish souls, and that the last eight pesukim, written by Moshe in tears, are an appendage to the Torah, as Adar Sheni is to the calendar. Haman thought the mazal of Adar was death, but did not know that the circle starts over.

title.en: Hidden nissim: the Bnei Yissaschar's parable

summary.en: The Mashgiach says our heel generation lives in a sea of hatred of Jews, yet Hashem's hand is visible as in the Megillah, which has no open nissim and not even His name. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar's parable of a dying patient whose medicine from China and doctor from America arrive at the last moment, to explain nissim within nature.

title.en: Everything just in time in the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the chain of events in the Megillah, from the feast of Achashverosh and Vashti's death to Bigsan and Seresh and Charbona's words, each insignificant alone but together a nes. He brings the Chiddushei HaRim's parable of a yeshiva that would have dismissed the news of Vashti as idle talk, and says today's events may yet be part of a future Megillah.

title.en: Reading the news like the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Hashem's name is hidden in the crevices of the Megillah and must be searched for. With a parable of a marionette show, he says the world's leaders are puppets on invisible strings, and that one who reads the Megillah correctly can see Hashem's name in the New York Times.

catalogTitle: הוא היצה"ר הוא השטן הוא ה"היינטיגע וועלט" איך זה נלמד מענינא דיומא

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains, from a saying of the Chasam Sofer and from Megillas Ruth, that 'today's world' is simply the newest name of the yetzer hara and the Satan, and that only firm separation from it carries a Jew through to Kabbalas HaTorah and Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a saying of the Chasam Sofer, heard through Rabbi Aharon Pollak: the yetzer hara's firm went bankrupt, reopened as 'Satan', and now trades under the name 'today's world'. He applies it to the son of the Egyptian, whose mother Shlomis greeted everyone, and to Akdamus, where Knesses Yisrael, the Shulamis, refuses the nations' invitation and wants only the separate camps of the desert. From Megillas Ruth he shows that the root of Moshiach was hidden in a generation of chutzpah and immorality, like the signs of ikvesa d'meshicha at the end of Sotah, and contrasts Ruth's honor for her mother-in-law with today's ideal of independence. From Rashi on the neighbors of Korach and of Moshe he shows how lasting an influence is. He calls for being 'extreme', saying 'I am a chassid', and closes with preparing from Rosh Chodesh Sivan for Kabbalas HaTorah.

en: According to the Chasam Sofer, the yetzer hara keeps changing its name, from yetzer hara to Satan to 'today's world', and a Jew held back from Hashem's will by 'today's world' should know it is the same firm.
Knesses Yisrael is the 'Shulamis', whose peace is within her own camp, unlike Shlomis bas Divri, who greeted everyone and let a foreign culture in.
Megillas Ruth describes a generation of chutzpah and immorality because the root of Moshiach was hidden there so that the Satan, who fears Moshiach, would not suspect it.
The neighbors one lives among shape a person for generations, as Rashi shows from the neighbors of Korach and of Moshe and Aharon.
The Mashgiach says the only way to withstand today's world is to separate from it and be 'extreme', to say openly 'I am a chassid'.
Matan Torah repeats every year, and from Rosh Chodesh Sivan one should follow, day by day, what happened then at Har Sinai.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer: the firm that changed its name

summary.en: After a word on preparing to speak, the Mashgiach tells how Rabbi Aharon Pollak heard from an elderly rebbetzin, a descendant of the Chasam Sofer, about his Shabbos-day mussar talks. Once the Chasam Sofer said that the yetzer hara's firm went bankrupt, reopened as 'Satan', and now calls itself 'today's world'.

title.en: Shlomis bas Divri and the son of the Egyptian

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the man of Dan objected to the son of the Egyptian pitching his tent in the camp, when the desert was wide. He answers from Rashi that his mother Shlomis greeted everyone, and the neighbor did not want her 'today's world' brought to his children.

title.en: Akdamus: Shulamis versus Shlomis

summary.en: From Akdamus and the Midrash on 'Shuvi shuvi haShulamis', the Mashgiach describes the nations inviting Knesses Yisrael into their society, and her answer that they cannot give her the separate camps of the desert. He contrasts Shlomis, who reaches out with peace to all, with Shulamis, whose peace is within her own walls.

title.en: Why Megillas Ruth tells of a corrupt generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads 'the days when the judges were judged' and Boaz sleeping at the edge of the grain heap, and asks why a megillah whose purpose is to establish David's lineage needs these details. He begins to answer that the Satan fears Moshiach, so Hashem hides every root of Moshiach.

title.en: Chutzpah and the hidden root of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the signs of ikvesa d'meshicha at the end of Sotah and explains that the ruling permitting a Moabite woman was a turning point for Moshiach, so it was hidden in a generation of chutzpah and immorality. In such a world Boaz noticed Ruth's tznius.

title.en: Ruth's honor for her mother-in-law

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Ruth, a princess of Moav, left everything to follow and serve her mother-in-law, against the sign of the end of days that a bride rises against her mother-in-law. He contrasts this with today's ideal of independence from parents and authority, and says the way to survive is separation, not greeting everyone.

title.en: The neighbor's influence lasts a thousand years

summary.en: From Rashi on the camps around the Mishkan, the Mashgiach shows that Reuven's neighbors learned from Korach while Yissachar, next to Moshe and Aharon, produced two hundred heads of Sanhedrin almost a thousand years later. He applies this to the pull of television and trends and to the broken families that come to him, all from 'today's world'.

title.en: Be 'extreme': I am a chassid

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls for separation, citing Yeshayahu's 'go into your rooms and shut your door', the Lubavitcher's blessing to be healthy, fresh and 'meshuga', and the Kotzker's advice to say 'I am a chassid'. He argues that today's world is the truly extreme one and describes what he saw in bungalow colonies as a young man and what goes on there now.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh Sivan: arriving at Har Sinai

summary.en: With Rosh Chodesh Sivan that night, the Mashgiach brings 'on this day they came to the desert of Sinai' and that leaving Refidim was with teshuvah, and the Avodas Yisrael's practice of learning each day what happened then. He explains that Matan Torah repeats every year, and brings the Rimanover that the five days before it were spent saying Ahavah Rabbah.

title.en: Preparing for Shavuos; closing blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach urges good learning and davening in the days before Shavuos and remembering Matan Torah from Rosh Chodesh on. He closes by blessing the listeners to stay healthy, fresh and settled, knowing that it is today's world that is mad, and to receive the Torah with joy.

catalogTitle: טעמים לאכילת מאכלי חלב. התעוררות לחג

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why the angels at Avraham's table were faulted for eating meat with milk and why milk is eaten on Shavuos, then teaches that every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah that Hashem writes anew each Shavuos, and that one prepares for it by making oneself clean and knowing that one is nothing.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the rewards the Mishnah in Avos promises one who learns Torah lishmah: counsel, kingship, the secrets of the Torah, and greatness over all creation, which he illustrates with stories of the Ba'al Shem Tov and of a wagon driver of the Stoliner Rebbe. From the angels' fear of Moshe he turns to the Midrash that Moshe silenced them by recalling that they ate meat and milk at Avraham's table, and asks how, since Rashi says the milk came first. Using the Chesed LeAvraham, a stringency of the Beis Yosef, and the Igros Sofrim's teaching that meat is din and milk a higher chesed, he resolves it through the argument over whether the upper or the lower prevails. He then explains milk on Shavuos, the renewal of the Torah each year, every Jew as a letter of the Sefer Torah reflected in the counting and camps of Bamidbar, and preparation through purity, humility and the strength of individuals.

en: The Mashgiach explains from the Mishnah in Avos that one who learns Torah lishmah is given counsel, a kingship that draws people to him, the secrets of the Torah, and greatness over all creation, even angels.
Meat is din and milk is chesed drawn from Binah, so meat after milk is permitted while milk after meat is not, because the lower food prevails.
Milk is eaten on Shavuos because the days of sefirah, days of din, have ended, and red has turned to white, din to chesed.
Each Shavuos the Torah is truly given again from heaven, and Hashem writes a new Sefer Torah in which every Jewish soul is a letter.
The preparation is to make oneself like clean white parchment, refining the animal side of the person, so the black fire of Hashem's letters can rest on it.
The Torah was given in the wilderness: knowing that one is nothing is the greatest preparation for receiving it.
In a generation where only individuals keep the Torah, each individual carries the Torah for all of Klal Yisrael.

title.en: The rewards of Torah lishmah

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the Mishnah in Avos on one who learns Torah lishmah: people draw counsel from him, he is given kingship and the secrets of the Torah, he becomes like a spring that grows stronger, and the Torah raises him above all creation.

title.en: Stories of a tzaddik's hidden power

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov saw that a shake of the Mishneh LaMelech's head cast down the heavenly minister of Russia, and how a wagon driver of the Stoliner Rebbe crossed breaking ice after calling out the name of a family. The heavenly ministers over roads, seas and ice tremble before one who learns Torah lishmah.

title.en: Did the angels eat meat with milk?

summary.en: From the angels' fear of Moshe, the Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Moshe answered them by recalling that they ate meat and milk at Avraham's table, and asks how, since Rashi says the milk came first. He brings the Chesed LeAvraham that the calf was made through Sefer Yetzirah and is not meat, and is left with two questions: why the angels were at fault, and why Avraham was not.

title.en: Din, chesed, and Moshe's answer to the angels

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that Avraham kept a stringency of not eating meat after milk in one meal, but without bread these were two meals. He brings the Igros Sofrim that meat is din and milk a strong chesed from Binah, so meat may follow milk since the lower prevails, and ties this to the argument between Moshe, who held that the lower prevails, and the angels, who held that the upper does.

title.en: Milk on Shavuos and the Torah given anew

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the reasons of the Rema and the Magen Avraham for eating milk on Shavuos: the days of sefirah are days of din, and as blood turns to milk, red turns to white. He then says that each Shavuos the Torah is truly given again, tells how the Shinever Rav saw it in Belz, and brings that the Shabbos before Shavuos contains all of Shavuos.

title.en: Bamidbar: every Jew is a letter

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Parshas Bamidbar is read before Shavuos: it counts the Jews, and every Jew has a letter in the Sefer Torah, as the word Yisrael hints. He brings the Arizal on seeing one's letter, the early sofrim who counted the letters, and Rabbi Akiva who expounded the crowns of each letter.

title.en: White parchment for Hashem's new Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says each Shavuos Hashem writes a new Sefer Torah, and no festival has as much preparation as Shavuos, from the counting of sefirah to Rosh Chodesh Sivan. He asks why a Sefer Torah must be written on an animal's hide and answers that the animal side of a person must be refined into clean white parchment for Hashem's black fire.

title.en: Counting by the root of the soul; the camps as a Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that only Moshe, Aharon and the nesi'im could count the Jews, because they saw each one's root and his letter in the Torah. The camps matched the books of the Torah with the Levi'im in the middle like Vayikra; an extra letter invalidates a Sefer Torah, which explains the incident of the blasphemer; and the 22,000 Levi'im, counted from thirty days, match the 22 letters.

title.en: Wilderness humility and the power of the individual

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the work of the Shabbos before Shavuos is to become clean by knowing one is nothing, since the Torah was given in the wilderness; he brings the Kozhnitzer that the fifty days can still be repaired at the last minute. He explains that the commandments were said in the singular so the Torah would endure through individuals, and says that today each individual must know his duty.

title.en: Receiving the Torah for the whole year

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads a passage on the hardships before Moshiach, when even rabbanim will need mercy to stay in emunah, and says that each Shavuos one receives the Torah for the whole year. He speaks of the purity of the night of Shavuos and the custom of going to the mikveh, of sleep and learning, and closes with a brachah.

catalogTitle: “זכור את יום אשר עמדת לפני ה' אלוקיך בחורב”

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the Torah's warning never to forget the day the Jewish people stood before Hashem at Chorev, and how that day returns every Shavuos to be received anew.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the pesukim in Devarim warning, in several expressions, not to forget the day at Chorev and to tell it to one's children: Har Sinai, where every Jew heard Hashem speak, is the foundation of emunah. He explains that every event in the Torah is engraved in its time, so each year the same lights return, and on Shavuos matan Torah comes down again, as tzaddikim visibly relived it; sin only insulates the body from feeling it. The avodah of Shavuos is to become a vessel for the Torah, especially at Ahavah Rabbah and the reading of the Aseres Hadibros. With the mashal of a chasan who pays for everything but forgets the ring, he warns against sleeping through the main moment after a night awake. He tells of the Belzer Rav's heart before Shavuos and the Satmar Rav's reading, stresses the worth of avodah in a polluted generation, and closes with the Midrash on the horns of Yitzchak's ram and a plea for mercy on all Jews.

en: The Torah warns in many expressions not to forget the day at Chorev, because Har Sinai, where every Jew heard Hashem, is the foundation of emunah passed on to the generations.
Every event in the Torah is engraved in its time, so each year the same lights return, and on Shavuos matan Torah comes down again.
The avodah of Shavuos is to be a vessel to receive the Torah, above all at the reading of the Aseres Hadibros, when every Jew stands at Har Sinai.
Staying awake all night is worthless if one then sleeps through Ahavah Rabbah and the reading of the Aseres Hadibros.
In a generation whose spiritual air is polluted, a Jew who struggles to learn and daven is doing something very great and precious to Hashem.
Having heard the left horn of the ram at Sinai, the Mashgiach asks that we soon hear the right horn, the shofar of Moshiach, and that Hashem have mercy on Jews everywhere.

the annual return of the Yomim Tovim
Shavuos night and the Aseres Hadibros
avodah in a spiritually polluted generation

title.en: Do not forget the day at Chorev

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the pesukim in Devarim that warn, in several expressions, not to forget the day the people stood before Hashem at Chorev and to tell it to one's children. He explains that Har Sinai, where every Jew became a prophet and heard Hashem speak face to face, is the foundation of emunah and of the belief in Moshe Rabbeinu.

title.en: The same lights return every year

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that everything in the Torah is engraved in its time like a circle, so each year the same lights return; this is why a year is called shanah, repetition. Tzaddikim such as the Sanzer Rav and Reb Sholom of Belz visibly relived matan Torah, and the Mashgiach says sin is like insulation that keeps the body from feeling what the soul experiences.

title.en: The avodah of Shavuos: becoming a vessel

summary.en: Every Yom Tov has its avodah, and the avodah of Shavuos is to become a vessel for the day at Chorev, which one must remember daily through the Six Remembrances or Ahavah Rabbah. The main receiving is at the reading of the Aseres Hadibros; the Mashgiach cites a Rebbe that one should fear Shavuos more than Rosh Hashanah, and describes the thunder and trembling at Sinai and the prayer for more Torah.

title.en: The chasan who forgot the ring

summary.en: The Mashgiach gives the mashal of a chasan who pays for everything at the wedding but refuses to buy the ring needed for the kiddushin, and compares him to one who stays up all Shavuos night and then sleeps through Ahavah Rabbah and the Aseres Hadibros. He advises resting a few hours before davening, and that one who knows he will fall asleep should not stay up all night.

title.en: The Belzer Rav's heart and a polluted generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Belzer Rav answered the king's doctor, who found his heart beating irregularly, that in six days it would be Shavuos, and recalls hearing the Satmar Rav read the Aseres Hadibros. Today we do not feel this, but since the physical air and water are polluted, so is the spiritual atmosphere, and a Jew who struggles to learn and daven in it is very precious.

title.en: The right horn of the ram and a plea for mercy

summary.en: From the Selichos prayer and the Midrash that the left horn of Yitzchak's ram was the shofar of Sinai and the right horn will be the shofar of Moshiach, the Mashgiach asks that we soon hear the right horn. He lists the dangers facing Jews in Eretz Yisroel, Russia and Iran, calls to pray for mercy on Shavuos, and urges coming to learn before davening and receiving the Torah with joy.

catalogTitle: A New יו”ט for Each Generation

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Purim is a new Yom Tov in every generation: Hashem hides behind nature, yet the Megillah's miracles are renewed each year, and Purim calls for bitachon against the fear and the 'coincidence' thinking of Amalek.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by calling Purim a great, misunderstood day that the Zohar compares to Yom Kippur, and says it should give Jews bitachon in current events. Purim is a Yom Tov of galus; the Jews then sinned by joining Achashverosh's feast, which celebrated his calculation that the seventy years had passed with no Beis Hamikdash. Unlike Pesach, Purim brings new miracles in every generation, hidden behind hester panim, the concealment of Hashem's face, which he finds today in the new Israeli government, global fear and weakened Yiddishkeit. Haman's power was fear; Mordechai and Esther answered it with bitachon. Citing the Arizal and the Chasam Sofer, he explains that the Megillah's light is greater because it came to a generation that had fallen so low. Purim is the reverse of Yom Kippur: the Shechinah descends to us. Finally he explains three meanings of Amalek's 'korcha', ending with Amalek's denial of hashgachah pratis and the historian Graetz's 'natural' account of the splitting of the sea.

en: Purim is not a one-time miracle like the Exodus; every year and every generation has its own new Purim and its own new Megillah.
Purim is a day of hester: Hashem hides, but He watches from behind the wall, and every detail of the Megillah and of current events is part of the miracle.
The main avodah of Purim is bitachon; Haman's power was to spread fear, and Mordechai and Esther overcame it by trusting Hashem.
The Megillah's light is greater because it was given at the end of the seventy years, in a time of ikvesa d'Meshicha and intermarriage like today; a deep pit needs a stronger light.
Yom Kippur and Purim share one purpose but work in opposite ways: on Yom Kippur Jews rise to Hashem, on Purim the Shechinah comes down to them in their lowliness.
Amalek's 'korcha' means he made the Jews impure, made them cold, and above all taught that everything is chance; Jews believe there is no such thing as coincidence.

candidateTopics: purim as a new yom tov in every generation

title.en: Purim, a great Yom Tov of galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is a misunderstood, very great day that the Zohar compares to Yom Kippur, and that it should give bitachon in current events. Purim is a Yom Tov of galus, and he explains the sin of joining Achashverosh's feast, which celebrated his calculation that the Beis Hamikdash would never be rebuilt.

title.en: A new Purim in every generation; today's hester

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Purim is a new Yom Tov for each generation, with a rerun of its miracles every year, and that every family and town has its Purim. Purim is hester, as the Gemara finds Esther in 'haster astir panai'; he describes today's hester in the new Israeli government's war on the chareidim and in the global fear.

title.en: Hashem peeks through the cracks

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how in a yeshiva class of about a hundred boys only one said Shir HaShirim before Shabbos, a sign of watered-down Yiddishkeit and itself part of the hester. Yet Hashem watches through the cracks, every detail of the Megillah and of today is part of the miracle, a Megillah is being written now, and the avodah is bitachon for the coming weeks.

title.en: Haman's fear and Esther's bitachon

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Haman's main klipah was spreading fear, and brings the child's passuk to Mordechai, 'do not fear sudden terror'. This year's double Adar is the month of decision; Mordechai did not bow, and Esther, feeling the Shechinah leave her, cried 'Keli Keli lama azavtani' and went to the king with mesirus nefesh and bitachon.

title.en: Why the Megillah's light is greater

summary.en: The Mashgiach says every year's events can be found in the Megillah, and brings the Chasam Sofer's Drashos that the light of Megillas Esther is greater than that of the Torah of Moshe. He explains it: the Megillah came at the end of the seventy years, in an ikvesa d'Meshicha full of intermarriage like today, and a deep pit needs a stronger light.

title.en: A new light: the Megillah of every year

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Arizal that the kedushah of Purim was a new revelation of Hashem never seen before, an 'ohr chadash', so each year's Megillah is new. One who reads it as an old story has not fulfilled the mitzvah, and the Megillah will remain in the days of Moshiach because its real story will be the last Purim before the geulah.

title.en: Yom Kippur rises, Purim descends; Amalek's chill

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Yom Kippur, when Jews rise to the heavens, with Purim, when the Shechinah comes down to them, all the more in Adar Sheni, which trails behind the camp like those Amalek attacked. He then explains 'asher korcha' as Amalek making the Jews impure and making them cold, without fire in learning and davening.

title.en: Amalek denies hashgachah pratis

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains a third meaning of 'korcha': Amalek denies hashgachah pratis, the first of the Rambam's principles. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's teaching on a falling leaf and warns that even one sentence of kefirah leaves a mark that takes years to remove.

title.en: Graetz and the splitting of the sea

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how as a boy he opened Graetz's history of the Jews and found it admits the splitting of the sea as a historical fact, witnessed by a whole nation. All the nations were frightened by it except Aluf Amalek, and Graetz explained it away as a natural event of tides and weather.

title.en: No coincidence: the Megillah's string of pearls

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers Graetz that such timing would itself be a greater miracle, like the miracle of the Megillah. Amalek, like Graetz, sees everything as natural chance, while Jews know there is no coincidence; Purim teaches emunah that every passuk of the Megillah is a pearl on one string, natural events over which we bless 'she'asah nissim'.

catalogTitle: כל יהודי הוא שליח מה'; שמירת עינים בימי הקיץ

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that every Jew is Hashem's messenger wherever he goes, and that the summer travel of Tamuz and Av is meant to repair the failed mission of the meraglim, above all by guarding the eyes and by tefillah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the meraglim, who set out on Rosh Chodesh Tamuz and returned on Tisha b'Av after failing their mission, and contrasts them with the successful messengers Yehoshua sent. He then asks why the whole world travels in exactly these weeks. Bringing the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'From Hashem are a man's steps established', he explains that every soul is sent down as a messenger, and that each person has a portion of creation that only he can repair: a glass of water in Chicago or a tree in the country has waited since creation for his brachah or his learning. Since the meraglim sinned with their eyes, these weeks are full of tests for the eyes; the Ba'al Shem Tov's reading of Bilaam's blind eye shows that forbidden sights blind a person to the light of Torah. The Mashgiach stresses tefillah for success, with a story of a tzaddik's Pesach, and calls on bochurim to keep learning and kabbalas ol in the summer, to see Hashem's creation, and so turn these months into joy.

en: According to the Ba'al Shem Tov, every person is a messenger of Hashem, and wherever he goes he has been sent there to do something.
The summer travel season falls in the meraglim's forty days, and a Jew's travels in these weeks are meant to repair what they spoiled.
Each person has his own portion of creation that only he can repair, through mitzvos and brachos, and spoil through aveiros.
The eyes are the most sensitive and holiest part of the body; one who looks at forbidden things can no longer see the light and sweetness of Torah.
Success in one's mission requires tefillah: the meraglim failed because they did not pray, while Yehoshua and Calev, who had tefillah, succeeded.
The summer is not ownerless time: one must keep learning and keep the yoke of Heaven, and the open countryside is a chance to see Hashem's creation and join its song.
Those who fulfill their mission turn Tamuz and Av into days of joy and bring Moshiach.

title.en: The meraglim's failed mission and Yehoshua's spies

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how the meraglim set out on Rosh Chodesh Tamuz and returned forty days later on Tisha b'Av with a bad report, bringing weeping for all generations. He notes that Shlach is read before Tamuz and that its haftarah and the Midrash contrast them with the successful messengers sent by Yehoshua.

title.en: Why the world travels; every man a messenger

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why everyone starts travelling from Rosh Chodesh Tamuz, and brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'From Hashem are a man's steps established': every soul is sent down from the Kisei HaKavod on a mission to bring back mitzvos. Most people fail like Moshe's meraglim, while tzaddikim succeed like Yehoshua's messengers.

title.en: Each person's portion of creation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Adam's sin spoiled all of creation, and that each of his descendants has a portion of the world to repair or spoil; in the generation of the Flood even the animals were corrupted, while Noach's animals and his portion, Eretz Yisrael, were spared. He gives the Ba'al Shem Tov's example of a businessman sent to Chicago so he can make a brachah on a glass of water that has waited since creation.

title.en: The bochur's summer mission in the country

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the reasons people give for travelling are only excuses: a bochur who goes to the country is sent there for a tree to learn under, a brook to make a brachah on, a beis medrash to daven in, or a pool where he must behave with tznius. If he fulfills this he is like Yehoshua's messengers; the meraglim made these days into days of mourning, and those who fulfill their mission turn them into joy and bring Moshiach.

title.en: Guarding the eyes: Bilaam's blind eye

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that because the meraglim sinned with their eyes, these weeks are full of tests for the eyes, and the eyes are the holiest part of the body. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's reconciliation of Rashi and Onkelos on Bilaam 'shesum ha'ayin': only his blind eye, never defiled, could see prophecy; so too one who guards his eyes sees the light of Torah. He adds the mitzvah of tzitzis, which brings holiness into the eyes.

title.en: Tefillah for success in the mission

summary.en: The Mashgiach says one must daven to Hashem to fulfill one's mission successfully, and tells of a tzaddik whose meticulous Pesach was spoiled by a grain of wheat in his soup; a dream-question revealed that he had not davened, and that a bird had dropped the kernel down the chimney. The meraglim failed for lack of tefillah, while Yehoshua, for whom Moshe davened, and Calev, who davened at Me'aras HaMachpelah, succeeded; from them come Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben Dovid.

title.en: Summer is not hefker: learning and kabbalas ol

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the summer months are hard for learning, yet they are not ownerless: a bochur may rest to gain strength, but must also learn in the summer and keep the yoke of Heaven, including in how he dresses. He tells of a bochur who threw off his yarmulke to run faster in a ball game, and contrasts him with one of the Slavita printers who stopped in the middle of running a gauntlet rather than go on without his yarmulke.

title.en: Joining creation's song; turning the months to joy

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Rambam that a person comes to love and fear of Hashem by seeing the wonders of creation, which in the city are hidden but in the country are open to see; all creation sings to Hashem, and a Jew joins the song by learning, davening and avoiding aveiros. He closes that the meraglim made Tamuz and Av sad months, and those who fulfill their mission will turn them into joy, as Zechariah says, and Moshiach will point to them.

catalogTitle: דרשה בלשון הקודש - משיח נטמן בימי בין המצרים - והעבודה לגלותו

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that under the orlah of the days of bein hamtzarim lies hidden the light of Moshiach, and that the work of every Jew, and especially of bochurim, is to remove that orlah from his heart through Torah, guarding the eyes and good middos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a question on Parshas Pinchas: why does the division of the land put Menashe before Ephraim and stress that Reuven is the firstborn, when the order of the degalim had changed? He then shows that bein hamtzarim hides great light under an orlah. Balak, a great klipah, carried the root of Moshiach through Ruth, so a parsha bears his name, and his own korbanos brought the salvation. Pinchas, who becomes Eliyahu, will remove the orlah from the whole world. The three weeks are the orlah of time. Tammuz and Av, the months of Reuven and Shimon, fell with them and will be first in the order of tikkun, which answers the opening question. He calls on the bochurim of Shiloh to remove the orlah of the heart through Torah and guarding the eyes, and closes with the hope that the fasts become festivals.

en: The three weeks are not only heavy days: they hold great lights, even Moshiach's birth on Tisha b'Av, covered by an orlah of mourning.
Wherever great tumah is found, it is a sign that great holiness lies beneath it.
Balak's korbanos, brought to destroy Israel, earned him Ruth and the root of Moshiach: the trouble itself becomes the salvation.
Pinchas, who becomes Eliyahu, is the angel of both the individual bris and the great milah that will remove the orlah from the whole world.
In bein hamtzarim the Torah returns to the order of tikkun, the birth order in which Reuven, Shimon and Menashe come first.
The task of every Jew in these days is to remove the orlah from his heart; when Israel does so below, Hashem removes the orlah from the world.
The bochurim of Shiloh carry the kedushah of Yosef, holiness of the eyes, which they must guard especially in Tammuz and Av.

order of the tribes and the months
Shiloh and the kedushah of Yosef

title.en: Menashe before Ephraim in Pinchas

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah lists Menashe before Ephraim when dividing the land, though Yaakov put Ephraim first, and why Pinchas repeats that Reuven is the firstborn after the order of the degalim had changed. He notes that the parshiyos from Balak onward are the parshiyos of bein hamtzarim.

title.en: Why Balak merited a parsha

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Nechemiah did not merit a sefer named for him, and asks why the wicked Balak did. Beneath Balak lies hidden goodness: from him came Ruth and the root of Moshiach. He adds the Rambam's proof of Moshiach from Parshas Balak and the Midrash that Moshiach was born on Tisha b'Av.

title.en: Great tumah hides great holiness

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets a rule: great tumah is a sign of holiness beneath it, as the bris is covered by orlah and as the Chazon Ish wrote of a troubled bochur. He applies it to Chevron and Shechem, the places of milah, and to bein hamtzarim, days in which, as the Maggid of Mezritch and the students of the Ba'al Shem Tov taught, a great hidden light can be reached.

title.en: Balak's korbanos and the root of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Balak saw that Moshiach would come from him and therefore wanted to destroy Israel. He reads 'ben Tzipor' as an allusion to Moshiach and shows that the very korbanos Balak brought to curse Israel earned him Ruth. From the pasuk 'es tzarah hi l'Yaakov u'mimenah yivashea' and the Arizal he concludes that the trouble itself is the salvation.

title.en: Even the wicked serve Hashem's honor

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Pharaoh had a merit, since through him came kiddush Hashem at the Yam Suf, and the pasuk that Hashem made everything for His sake, even the wicked. He brings the Gemara on learning not for its own sake from Balak's korbanos, and Michah's call to remember what Balak advised. He reads 'yoshev mimuli' as Balak's fear that Israel would cut off his orlah, and turns to Pinchas.

title.en: Pinchas, Eliyahu and the milah of the world

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings two midrashim on Pinchas's 'bris shalom': that he becomes Eliyahu, herald of the geulah, and that he becomes the angel of the bris at every milah. He reconciles them: milah is both individual and general, the removal of orlah from the whole world, of which Esav is the root. He then shows from Sefer Yetzirah that the three weeks are the orlah of time, with hidden light beneath, which is why Eliyahu appears on Shabbos Pinchas.

title.en: Two orders of the tribes; Tammuz and Av

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the tribes have an order of tikkun, by birth, and an order of kilkul, the degalim after the sin, in which Reuven lost his place. Every month corresponds to a tribe; Reuven and Shimon, fourth and fifth in the degalim, are Tammuz and Av, and when they fell, these months fell into the klipos. In the future every kilkul will return to its tikkun.

title.en: Aharon's stones and Reuven's holiness

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that even after the egel, the names on Aharon's shoulder stones follow the birth order, because Aharon, who enters the Kodesh HaKodashim, represents Israel in its state of tikkun. He explains the holiness of Reuven, Yaakov's first strength, and says that Tammuz and Av, the months of Reuven and Shimon, will in the future be raised above all months.

title.en: The opening question answered; Balak's hidden number

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers his opening question: in bein hamtzarim the Torah speaks of dividing the land in the order of tikkun, so Reuven is the firstborn and Menashe comes before Ephraim. He returns to Balak, whose parsha is named for the hidden good in him, and explains the importance of gematria and the milui, the hidden part of a letter's name, which in Balak points to Moshiach.

title.en: Removing the orlah of the heart

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the task of every Jew whom Hashem has touched in these days is to remove the orlah from his heart, as the Torah says 'u'maltem es orlas levavchem'; when Israel does this, Hashem removes the orlah from the world. He tells the bochurim they are Israel's true army, and that the miracles seen in the wars with the Arabs and the Gulf War came through the protection of Torah.

title.en: Jerusalem is decided in heaven

summary.en: The Mashgiach says everything revolves around Jerusalem, and that no prime minister decides what will be there: Hashem judges the princes above before the kings below. The strife over Jerusalem below is a sign of a judgment in heaven, perhaps that the time has come for Jerusalem to return, with the nations' angels accusing. The answer, he says, is teshuvah: the Torah of the bochurim and tzedakah, through which Moshiach will come.

title.en: Shabbos Chazon and the third Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Kedushas Levi that on Shabbos Chazon Hashem shows every Jew the third Beis HaMikdash, and shows that the hidden letters of 'Tisha b'Av' hint to the third Beis HaMikdash. He explains from the Zohar that Shabbos mincha is the highest time, and that the Shabbosos of bein hamtzarim, especially Shabbos Chazon, are wholly like it; each one reaches it according to his preparation during the week.

title.en: Shiloh, Yosef and guarding the eyes

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the bochurim that learning in Shiloh shows their souls belong to Shiloh and to the kedushah of Yosef, holiness of the eyes. He brings the Gemara that in Shiloh kodashim were eaten wherever it could be seen, unlike Jerusalem, and explains that Tammuz and Av are the two eyes. In the time of ikvesa d'Meshicha the bochurim must guard their eyes, especially in these months; he adds that Shiloh is the place of zivugim and that Hashem and Knesses Yisrael are the chassan and kallah.

title.en: Sefer Bamidbar ends with a wedding

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that entering the nine days we finish Bamidbar, which ends with the marriages of the daughters of Tzelafchad, and brings Tosafos in Gittin that there is no gap between Bamidbar and Devarim: there is no divorce, rather a holy zivug. Devarim opens with rebuke as a badchan rebukes a chassan before the chuppah. He closes that Tisha b'Av will become a festival, that the knife to remove the orlah is in the bochurim's hands, and with a tefillah for the geulah.

catalogTitle: התהפכות של חדשי תמוז ואב

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Tammuz and Av, months of harsh judgment and churban, hide under their kelipah the greatest light of Moshiach, and that through toiling in Torah one can cut away that covering and turn the curse into a blessing.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Tammuz as a month of strong judgment, the reversed form of Hashem's name, tied to the meraglim and to the tribes of Reuven and Shimon. Yet the navi Zechariah promises that these fasts will become days of joy, and he brings hints that redemption is born in them: Aharon's 'chag laHashem machar', Boaz's wedding to Ruth on 17 Tammuz, and Moshiach's birth on Tisha b'Av. The rule is that the greater the kedushah, the thicker its orlah. The three nations not yet conquered, Amon, Moav and Edom, and Balak, ancestor of Moshiach who tried to hold him captive, show the same pattern in place and in soul; Tammuz and Av show it in time. Hashem turned Bilaam's curse into a blessing, and so a struggling bochur should know his thick orlah hides a great soul. Like Osniel ben Kenaz, who conquered by restoring forgotten halachos, one conquers these days through learning, guarding the eyes, and fulfilling one's shlichus without fear.

en: Tammuz and Av are months of strong judgment, linked to the sin of the meraglim and to tribes and nesi'im who stumbled.
According to Zechariah the fasts of the fourth and fifth months will become days of joy, and these days already carry the roots of redemption.
The greater a kedushah, the thicker the kelipah or orlah that surrounds it, like the orlah over the bris and the harsh nations of Eretz Yisrael.
Balak was the ancestor of Moshiach through Ruth, and as a great kelipah he tried to keep Moshiach captive within himself.
Each part of Eretz Yisrael holds a part of the Torah, so conquering it means revealing its halachos, and learning Torah in Tammuz and Av conquers these days.
Tammuz and Av correspond to the eyes, and guarding the eyes prepares a person to see the hidden light of the Torah.
Every Jew is a shliach of Hashem, and these months call on the bochurim to fulfill their shlichus without fear, as Kalev and Pinchas did.

title.en: Tammuz, a month of strong judgment

summary.en: After a word of thanks, the Mashgiach explains that Tammuz carries Hashem's name in reverse order and is a month of harsh judgment, harsher than Av. He links the month to Reuven, who was not blessed by Yaakov, and to the two nesi'im who stumbled, at Korach's congregation and at the deed of Zimri.

title.en: Days of churban destined to be festivals

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the days from the sending of the meraglim as low days of churban, then brings Zechariah's promise that the fasts will turn to joy. He adds Aharon's 'chag laHashem machar', the Chasam Sofer's reckoning that Boaz married Ruth on 17 Tammuz, and the Midrash that Moshiach is born on Tisha b'Av.

title.en: Great kedushah, thick orlah

summary.en: The Mashgiach states the rule that the greater the kedushah, the stronger the kelipah guarding it, as with the orlah over the bris and the harsh nations of Eretz Yisrael, and applies it to Tammuz and Av. He tells how the Plantcher Rebbe made a kind of kiddush on Tisha b'Av, saying it will be a Yom Tov when Moshiach comes.

title.en: The three nations Moshiach will conquer

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that of the ten nations promised to Avraham, Yehoshua conquered seven, while Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, Amon, Moav and Edom, await Moshiach. Moshe's conquest of Sichon and Og in the Tammuz parshiyos was only a beginning, and the Mashgiach calls on serious Jews to break the kelipah of these months, whose parshiyos all herald redemption.

title.en: Balak, grandfather of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Nechemiah, who lost a sefer in his name, with Balak, who merited a parsha because his korbanos brought Ruth into the world. Balak sensed Moshiach would come from him and as a great kelipah tried to hold him back; the Ohr HaChaim reads 'ben Tzipor' as a hint to Moshiach, the bird waiting in its heavenly chamber.

title.en: Place, soul and time: the hidden Moshiach

summary.en: Using the Sefer Yetzirah idea that whatever exists in time also exists in soul and place, the Mashgiach sets Balak as the soul, Amon and Moav as the place and Tammuz and Av as the time where Moshiach lies hidden under an orlah. He brings 'v'hu yoshev mimuli', the Gemara's two doves, Ruth and Naamah, and the Rambam that Moshiach must come from David and Shlomo.

title.en: Curse turned to blessing; Osniel's conquest

summary.en: From 'vayahafoch Hashem Elokecha lecha es haklalah livrachah' the Mashgiach tells the bochur who struggles that a thick orlah is a sign of a great soul beneath it, to be cut away with teshuvah, hasmadah, tefillah and middos. He then explains how Osniel ben Kenaz conquered Kiryas Sefer by restoring through pilpul the halachos forgotten after Moshe's passing, since each part of Eretz Yisrael holds a part of the Torah.

title.en: Conquering Tammuz and Av through Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies this to the present: whoever sits and learns with iyun in Tammuz and Av, bringing out halachos, conquers a part of Eretz Yisrael and may help free Moshiach, as Moshe conquered Sichon and Og through his toil in Torah. He brings that 'haklalah livrachah' equals talmud Torah in gematria, the Avodas Yisroel that in bein hametzarim one can reach the Shechinah, and 'ki rabim bnei shomemah' about the souls of the last generations.

title.en: The eyes of Tammuz and Av

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes today's new kelipos, the internet and the cell phone, that take the power of chiddush away from Torah, and says Torah must be earned to reveal its hidden light. Since Tammuz and Av correspond to the eyes, he calls for guarding the eyes, so that they can see the ohr haganuz of the Torah.

title.en: Months of shlichus; the call to the bochurim

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Tammuz and Av months of shlichus: the meraglim failed in theirs, while Kalev and Pinchas succeeded, and every Jew is sent by Hashem on a shlichus. The months beg the bochurim to redeem them through learning, as pidyon shevuyim, to go without fear like Kalev who davened in Chevron, and he closes with a brachah that the two months turn to blessing.

catalogTitle: ממוכן Awakens the Merit of the לחם הפנים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why Memuchan, who is Haman, has a heavenly counterpart pleading with the merit of the lechem hapanim: the bread that stayed warm shows that Hashem's love for even the rejected Jews never grows cold, and that is the miracle of Purim.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Rokeach linking Purim to the lechem hapanim, and the Gemara that the names of Achashverosh's advisers are angels pleading with the merits of the korbanos, the last, Memuchan, with the lechem hapanim, though Memuchan is Haman. He explains that Amalek attacked the cast-outs of Shevet Dan, and that their surplus silver went for the hooks of the pillars, outside the kedushah, which is why Moshe forgot them. The ben ish Mitzri mocked the lechem hapanim, holding like Amalek that Hashem's love for Dan had gone stale. The Mashgiach answers that every Jew has a hidden point that is never a rasha, shown by the two identical goats of Yom Kippur and the Rambam's 'I want'. Haman's ten thousand talents matched only the main half-shekels and ignored the surplus; that surplus neutralized him. Purim is the Yom Tov of the plain Jew, and the Mashgiach ends with this year's three-day Purim in Yerushalayim and a call for tzedakah.

en: According to the Gemara, Memuchan's heavenly counterpart pleads with the merit of the lechem hapanim, and Memuchan is Haman; the shiur sets out to explain the connection.
Amalek attacked the cast-outs of Shevet Dan, who were outside the Clouds of Glory, and Hashem's anger at Amalek is the greatest because they started with His children.
The surplus silver of the half-shekel, given by the Jews who were outside, went for the hooks of the pillars, the one part of the Mishkan outside the kedushah, which is why Moshe Rabbeinu forgot it.
The warm lechem hapanim shows that Hashem's love for every tribe, even Dan, never becomes stale; the ben ish Mitzri who denied the miracle sided with Amalek.
Every Jew has a hidden point, rooted in Avraham Avinu, where he is not a rasha; this is why the two goats of Yom Kippur must be identical.
Haman's ten thousand talents matched only the 600,000 half-shekels, not the surplus of the rejected, and that surplus is what nullified his decree.
Purim is the Yom Tov of the simple Jew, celebrating only that he is a Yid, and in the lowest generations it grows greater.

title.en: Memuchan and the lechem hapanim

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is misunderstood and greater in a way than Yom Kippur. He brings the Rokeach linking Purim to the lechem hapanim and the Gemara that Memuchan's heavenly counterpart pleads with the lechem hapanim, and asks why, since Memuchan is Haman.

title.en: Amalek and the cast-outs of Dan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem's anger at Amalek exceeds that at any other nation because Amalek attacked the idol-worshipping cast-outs of Shevet Dan, who were outside the Clouds of Glory. Hashem's answer is that they are still His children.

title.en: The forgotten silver of the hooks

summary.en: From the reckoning in Parshas Pekudei, the Mashgiach shows that the 600,000 half-shekels went for the sockets and the surplus for the hooks of the pillars, which were outside the kedushah. He reasons that this surplus came from the rejected of Dan, which is why Moshe Rabbeinu forgot it until he was reminded.

title.en: The ben ish Mitzri and the warm bread

summary.en: Following Rashi, the Mashgiach describes how the ben ish Mitzri mocked the lechem hapanim, which stayed warm for nine days, and insisted on a place in Dan's camp. He explains the dispute: the neighbors argued from the twelve separately baked loaves, each dear to Hashem and kept warm, that Dan is not rejected, while he denied the miracle and so took Amalek's position.

title.en: The hidden point in every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that every Jew has an inextinguishable point where he is not a rasha, citing the Ba'al Shem Tov, Reb Tzadok HaKohen on the two identical goats of Yom Kippur and on Yaakov and Esav, and the Rambam on a forced 'I want'. Yom Kippur and Purim both bring this inner will to the surface.

title.en: Haman's silver and the surplus

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Tosafos that Haman's ten thousand talents matched the half-shekels of the 600,000 and asks why Haman did not pay for the surplus. He answers that Haman, like Amalek, discounted the rejected Jews, and their surplus silver came first and nullified his shekalim; Purim is thus the Yom Tov of the plain Jew.

title.en: Haman as the Mitzri, and our generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Yaaros Devash that Haman was a gilgul of the Mitzri whom Moshe killed and Mordechai a gilgul of Moshe, and adds that the ben ish Mitzri therefore shared Haman's view. He returns to the lechem hapanim as proof of the hidden point, and suggests that today's generation are gilgulim of Shevet Dan.

title.en: The Yom Tov of the rejected

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is the Yom Tov of the rejected, whose joy is simply being a Yid, as Mordechai would not bow because he was a Yid. He contrasts milah, the point of the Jew, with tefillin, the mitzvos, says Purim has both, and that each Purim grows greater as the generations fall lower.

title.en: Three-day Purim and a call for tzedakah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes this year's three-day Purim in Yerushalayim, which Shabbos magnifies, and says it reaches all of Klal Yisrael at a time of danger with no natural solution. He closes by urging the listeners to rest, hear every word of the Megillah, and give more tzedakah than they can, since the miracle came through the extra silver.

catalogTitle: ביאור בענין פרשיות מחוברים - נחיצות האחדות בימי בין המצרים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that parshiyos are joined only at times that call for repairing the sin of baseless hatred, and that each group of Jews may keep its own way as a family, not as a party, while loving every Jew.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with parshas Masei, which repeats Aharon's passing and adds that it was on Rosh Chodesh Av. Aharon, the Kohen Gadol, embodied the Beis Hamikdash, so his passing is a churban, read on the Shabbos that blesses Av. He then explains that every Jew is a letter of the Torah and that souls come in families, like the sedros of the year, each with its own Shabbos and each shevet with its own nusach. Yet at times of hoped-for redemption or of repairing baseless hatred, in Nissan, Tishrei, Sefirah and the Three Weeks, two parshiyos are joined. Through Kamtza and Bar Kamtza he shows how two people making peace could have saved Yerushalayim. Praising the refinement he finds in Stolin, he warns that chassidus must be a family, not a party, and closes with Aharon, the lover of peace, and the call to strengthen brotherhood in the month of Av.

en: Aharon the Kohen Gadol embodied the Beis Hamikdash, so the Torah's mention of his passing on Rosh Chodesh Av speaks of the churban.
Every Jew is a letter of the Torah, and souls belong to families, as each sedra has its own Shabbos and each shevet its own nusach.
Parshiyos are joined only before Nissan and Tishrei, in Sefirah and in the Three Weeks, the times of hoped-for geulah or of repairing baseless hatred.
Had Kamtza and Bar Kamtza made peace, two people could have tipped all of Yerushalayim to merit and prevented the churban.
Chassidus must be a family, not a party: a party says the truth is only with me, a family knows the other is also a family.
Aharon, lover and pursuer of peace, is the Beis Hamikdash, and the work of the month of Av is to strengthen brotherhood among Jews.
