title.en: Why Masei repeats Aharon's passing

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why parshas Masei repeats Aharon's passing, adding the date Rosh Chodesh Av, and why it says only that the Kenaani 'heard'. He answers that Aharon the Kohen Gadol was the Beis Hamikdash itself, so his passing is a form of churban.

title.en: Masei as galus; Aharon's years as the Mikdash

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the journeys of Masei hint at the four exiles and that every Jew passes through them by Divine providence; the parsha is read on the Shabbos before Av. He then maps Aharon's 123 years onto the Mishkan's thirty, twenty and ten amos, and says his passing on Rosh Chodesh Av is the root of Tisha B'Av.

title.en: Letters, families and separate shevatim

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that every Jew is a letter of the Torah and that souls come in families that were together at the Kisei Hakavod and at Sinai. As each sedra has its own Shabbos, each shevet has its own nusach and customs, yet good ways may flow from one shevet to another.

title.en: When parshiyos are joined

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed through baseless hatred, so at certain times unity must be stressed. Parshiyos are joined before Nissan and Tishrei, the months of geulah, and in Sefirah and the Three Weeks, to repair the lack of unity; at other times each Shabbos stands alone.

title.en: My nusach, and the other is also a shevet

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew should have his own nusach and Rebbe, but must know that the other is also a shevet of Klal Yisroel. He brings the Divrei Chaim on a chassid who says only his Rebbe is a Rebbe, and the dispute of shlishi and shishi, going back to the sea arguing with Moshe at Krias Yam Suf.

title.en: Kamtza and Bar Kamtza

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how two people could destroy Yerushalayim. He brings the Maharal that they were a sign of baseless hatred, and adds that all souls form one rope, so a fault below pulls down above, and that one act can tip the whole world. Had the two made peace over a l'chaim, the churban would have been averted.

title.en: Refinement: Stolin and Yehuda

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why he speaks of this here: in Stolin people are refined. He brings that Yehuda left his pledge with Tamar rather than take it back, because he was a refined man, and through this the kingship of Yehuda and Moshiach came.

title.en: A family, not a party; Aharon and Av

summary.en: The Mashgiach says chassidus in some ways became a party, which the Ba'al Shem Tov never intended, and contrasts a party, which holds that only it has the truth, with a family. He returns to Aharon's passing and the Kenaani's hearing: Av corresponds to Shimon, the 'hearing' went into galus, and Aharon, lover of peace, brought Jews together.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh gatherings and the call for unity

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that when Av comes, Jews sit together at seudos to strengthen brotherhood and renew the beauty of chassidus as a family. He urges that one group could be the one to bring Moshiach, explains why he spoke, and closes with a brachah that Tisha B'Av turn to joy.

catalogTitle: בשבת חזון נתגלה השמחה של ט' באב לעתיד וכל יהודי רואה בית השלישי בבנינה. ביאור ענין שמיטה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Three Weeks are the hidden, still-unconquered 'territory of Esav' in time, that Shabbos Chazon already lets every Jew see the future consolation, and that shemittah, like Shabbos and Yerushalayim, makes every Jew a kohen who lives on Hashem's blessing.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Moshe's rebuke over the white manna: white draws down chessed, free sustenance like an infant's milk. Moshe prayed to enter 'the good mountain and the Levanon', the place of whiteness, against the red din of Edom. Hashem told him to turn 'tzafonah', to the hidden Torah. The ten nations promised to Avraham include three still unconquered, Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, which correspond to the Three Weeks, the boundary of Esav in time; therefore simcha cannot yet enter, and Shabbos Chazon is the highest of them. Yet Shabbos, with its tosefes, reaches past that boundary, so every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash. Moshe's conquest of Sichon and Og earned him Sefer Devarim, the 'Shabbos' and shemittah of the Torah. The Mashgiach then develops Shabbos, shemittah and Yerushalayim as one idea: nobody owns, Hashem gives, every Jew becomes a kohen. He ends with the three who said 'eicha' and Shabbos Chazon as an aufruf before the great wedding.

en: White draws down chessed: the manna was white because the generation of the desert received its sustenance freely, like an infant, outside the curse of 'by the sweat of your brow'.
The three unconquered nations, Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, correspond to the Three Weeks, which are Esav's boundary in time; simcha cannot yet be brought into them.
Shabbos, the source of blessing and of tosefes, can enter Esav's boundary, so on Shabbos Chazon every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash and the consolation of Tzion.
Sefer Devarim, Moshe's own part of the Torah, is the seventh book, the Shabbos and shemittah of the Torah, earned through conquering Sichon and Og, the tosefes of Eretz Yisroel.
Shemittah teaches that Hashem, not man, is the owner; Yerushalayim, which was never divided among the tribes, is a constant shemittah, and in the seventh year it spreads over all of Eretz Yisroel.
In the shemittah year every Jew becomes like a kohen whose inheritance is Hashem: he lifts his eyes from the earth, learns Torah and trusts that sustenance comes from Hashem.

In the future all Jews will be kohanim, all of Eretz Yisroel will be Yerushalayim, and the whole world a day that is entirely Shabbos; great souls like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Eliyahu already live in that state.

title.en: Why the white manna drew Moshe's rebuke

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Moshe's rebuke over the complaint about the white manna and explains that each color draws down a different light; white draws chessed, as seen in white garments of doctors and kohanim. Like an infant's white milk, the manna was white because the desert generation received free sustenance outside the curse of 'by the sweat of your brow'.

title.en: The Levanon against the redness of Edom

summary.en: Moshe asked how they could complain about food given in chessed, and then himself prayed in chessed to enter 'the good mountain and the Levanon', the Beis HaMikdash, the place of whiteness. Edom is red, the side of din; the Mashgiach contrasts Esav's craving for red with the future when Hashem comes from Edom in red garments.

title.en: Turn north: the hidden Torah and the heel generation

summary.en: Moshe is told 'turn northward', which the Mashgiach reads as turning to the Torah, called 'tzafun', hidden. Esav's land is not given 'until the sole of the foot': not the great generations of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and Rabbi Akiva but the lowest generation, the heel of Moshiach, will merit judging Mount Esav, and the three last nations promised to Avraham.

title.en: Three matzos, three nations, three weeks

summary.en: The three matzos under the Seder plate correspond to Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, that is Ammon, Moav and Seir; Moshe, the middle matzah, reached Moav, while Seir awaits Moshiach. The seven conquered nations correspond to the seven weeks of consolation, which are within reach, while the three hidden ones correspond to the Three Weeks, the greatest Shabbosos of the year whose light is still beyond grasp.

title.en: Esav's boundary in time: no simcha yet

summary.en: Seir refused to let Moshe pass, because Esav does not yet concede the blessings to Yaakov, and 'I will not give you of their land'. The same boundary exists in time: the Three Weeks, with Shabbos Chazon as Kadmoni, their highest, are Esav's province, where one may not bring in Yisroel's simcha; therefore tzaddikim said even a smile on Tisha b'Av is dangerous, while Yerushalayim is the source of all simcha.

title.en: Shabbos Chazon: every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: Shabbos is different: the satan has no hold on it, and like the matzah eaten on Shabbos erev Pesach it gives a measure of grasp even now. The Mashgiach brings the teaching attributed to the Kedushas Levi that on Shabbos Chazon every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash, with the parable of the father who shows his son a third, beautiful garment, and explains 'chazon' as seeing with the heart.

title.en: Shabbos as source of blessing and tosefes

summary.en: From the Pri Tzaddik: the blessings of the week lie in its Shabbos, and since Tisha b'Av is the birth of Moshiach, that birth already lies in Shabbos Chazon. Shabbos is the source of blessing, and blessing means increase; tosefes Shabbos spreads beyond its borders, which is why Shabbos can enter Esav's boundary. The Three Weeks are days of 'orlah' covering a great holiness, the Name hidden in 'mi ya'aleh lanu hashamaymah'.

title.en: Removing the orlah: Torah conquers Eretz Yisroel

summary.en: The seven nations were an orlah covering Eretz Yisroel, so the land was promised in the parsha of milah and Yehoshua circumcised the people before entering. Osniel ben Kenaz conquered Kiryas Sefer and through his pilpul restored the forgotten halachos hidden there; so every piece of Torah learned with toil conquers a part of Eretz Yisroel. The land of Sichon and Og, given to Gad and Reuven, is the tosefes, 'chelkas mechokek', Moshe's portion.

title.en: Sefer Devarim: the Shabbos and shemittah of the Torah

summary.en: Following the Pri Tzaddik, Sefer Devarim stands between the Written and Oral Torah: Moshe said it on his own and was then told to write it. He merited it after conquering Sichon and Og; counting 'Vayehi binso'a' as a separate book, Devarim is the seventh book, the Shabbos and shemittah of the Torah. Moshe then thought the world had reached Shabbos and the decree was annulled, since shemittah, like Shabbos, has a tosefes.

title.en: Shabbos, shemittah and Yerushalayim: nobody is owner

summary.en: As the six weekdays prepare for Shabbos, Eretz Yisroel prepares for Yerushalayim, whose produce is brought there; Yerushalayim is the moon and malchus, with nothing of its own. Shemittah teaches that Hashem is the owner, as Shabbos teaches that Hashem creates; Yerushalayim, where nothing is planted and which was not divided among the tribes, is always shemittah, and in the seventh year spreads over the whole land. Both are for the poor, and for sitting and learning.

title.en: The shemittah Jew becomes a kohen

summary.en: After shemittah one goes up to Yerushalayim to learn; the true 'festival of gathering' is the gathering of Torah and of Yisroel, Hashem's harvest. A farmer looks down to the earth for his crop, but shemittah tells him to lift his eyes, for his inheritance is Hashem; the Mashgiach announces that the shemittah year is now coming, when every Jew should become a kohen who learns and trusts in Hashem.

title.en: Twelve tribes, Yaakov and the future kingdom of kohanim

summary.en: Eretz Yisroel was divided into twelve portions like the twelve months; Yaakov, above the tribes, is Shabbos, and Yerushalayim is his city. So on weekdays one asks twelve blessings in Shemoneh Esrei, but on Shabbos one middle blessing for being a Shabbos Jew. In the future Yerushalayim will spread over the land, all Jews will be a kingdom of kohanim, and there will be white, the Levanon, not Esav's red.

title.en: Eating 'atika': Shabbos meal and shemittah

summary.en: On 'what will we eat in the seventh year' the Torah answers 'you will eat the old', which the Targum renders 'atika', as on Shabbos one eats the meal of Atika Kadisha; the Mashgiach tells of the Beis Aharon and a simple chassid who relished Shir HaShirim without knowing its meaning. Some great souls, like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai whom the Zohar calls Shabbos, live in constant shemittah; hence his view in Berachos and the halacha following him in Maseches Shabbos.

title.en: Eliyahu the kohen in the cemetery

summary.en: In the future the halacha will follow Rabbi Shimon; Shabbos and Yerushalayim need no sanctification by a court, and shemittah is forgiveness. The Mashgiach tells how Rabbah bar Avuha found Eliyahu in a non-Jewish cemetery and asked whether he was not a kohen; Eliyahu answered with Rabbi Shimon's view. Since Eliyahu, of the tribe of Gad, already lives in the days of Moshiach when all Jews are kohanim, he answered by the halacha of that time.

title.en: Three who said 'eicha': Shabbos Chazon as an aufruf

summary.en: The Midrash says three prophets said 'eicha', Moshe, Yeshayahu and Yirmiyahu, and all three come together on Shabbos Chazon in the parsha, haftarah and Eicha; they are the shoshvinin who lead to the wedding in Yerushalayim, so Shabbos Chazon is an aufruf. The Mashgiach closes that one should use this Shabbos to sew the garments, accept the yoke of kehunah, Torah and bitachon for the shemittah year, and merit the garments of the redemption.

oneLiner.en: On the yahrzeit of the Arizal, the Mashgiach says that the counsel for the last generation is tefillah, and calls for lively, united davening together with the chazzan.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed only to our eyes: its kedushah remains, as the Rambam rules about the holiness of the Temple site, and Tisha B'Av was meant to be a great Yom Tov. He then explains that in earlier generations a person's tefillah was weighed by his Torah, while in a weak generation Hashem accepts tefillah according to the state of the generation. He notes that davening has recently weakened and calls for lively davening, together with the chazzan, like the angels who sing as one, and with a raised voice that the Shulchan Aruch says awakens kavanah. Turning to the Arizal's yahrzeit, he says the Arizal came down to guide the last generation, and he brings the Toldos Aharon Rebbe's lively davening. A story of Mordechai's fast over Pesach leads to a reason for quiet davening on Tisha B'Av. He ends that whatever is weak needs chizuk, and that learning and davening pull each other.

en: The Mashgiach says the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed only as it appears to us; its kedushah remains, as the Rambam rules about the Temple site.
In a weak generation Hashem accepts tefillah according to the state of the generation, not by the measure of earlier, Torah-filled times.
The Mashgiach calls for lively davening, together with the chazzan, so that each person feels part of the whole of Klal Yisroel, like the angels who sing as one.
The Arizal, whose teachings were for great mekubalim, also came down to guide the last generation, and the counsel for that generation is tefillah.
Whatever area of avodah has weakened needs chizuk, and learning and davening each pull the other along.

candidateTopics: tefillah as the counsel for the last generation
kedushah of the Beis HaMikdash after the churban

title.en: The kedushah of the Mikdash and tefillah today

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed only to our eyes, that its kedushah remains as the Rambam rules, and that Tisha B'Av was meant to be a great Yom Tov. He then explains that in a weak generation Hashem accepts tefillah according to the generation's state.

title.en: Lively davening, all together

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that davening has weakened and calls for lively tefillah together with the chazzan, like the angels who sing as one. He says this united tefillah is the one the Arizal spoke of for the last generation, and brings the Shulchan Aruch that a raised voice awakens kavanah.

title.en: The Arizal's yahrzeit and his guidance

summary.en: On the Arizal's yahrzeit the Mashgiach says one connects to him through his Torah, and that the Arizal also came down to guide the last generation. He tells how the Toldos Aharon Rebbe urged lively davening even on Tisha B'Av, and says that we must follow the Shulchan Aruch.

title.en: Mordechai's fast, Tisha B'Av, and chizuk

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a story of Mordechai's fast over Pesach and suggests from it a reason for quiet davening on Tisha B'Av. He then explains that whatever has weakened needs chizuk, that learning and davening pull each other, and closes on the joy in heaven at a gathering of chizuk on the Arizal's yahrzeit.

catalogTitle: מרדכי and אסתר Rectified the חטא עץ הדעת

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the root of Adam's sin, of the Golden Calf and of the error at Achashverosh's feast was not waiting, that Mordechai came to repair it, and that on Purim and in Parshas Parah Hashem reaches even the Jews who stand outside.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rashi's account of the Golden Calf: the people counted Moshe's forty days from the day he went up, and erred. Why could they not apply the rule that part of a day counts as a whole? Through the Bnei Yissaschar's teaching that a mikveh's forty se'ah hold 960 lugin, and that Matan Torah is a rebirth like a mikveh, he shows that 960 full hours were needed. Every mistake has a root: the people did not wait, just as Adam did not wait for Shabbos to make Kiddush from the Tree of Knowledge. The same error recurred when the Jews miscounted the seventy years and went to Achashverosh's feast, while Mordechai warned them to wait. The Mashgiach applies this to waiting for Moshiach today. He then discusses the five final letters, Haman's shekalim, the forgotten hooks of the pillars, the rejected Jews of the tribe of Dan, Tehillim 34, and Parshas Parah as a salvation reaching those who are outside.

en: Matan Torah was a rebirth like immersion in a mikveh, so it required forty complete days of 24 hours, 960 hours matching the 960 lugin of a mikveh; the rule that part of a day counts as a whole does not apply.
The root of the error at the Golden Calf, and of Adam's sin before it, was not waiting: Adam should have waited for Shabbos to make Kiddush over the juice of the Tree of Knowledge.

The Jews who went to Achashverosh's feast repeated the same mistake: they thought the seventy years had passed without redemption, while Mordechai warned them to wait, making him a repair of Adam's sin.
The Mashgiach says the task of our generation is to wait for Moshiach and not to think that the redemption has already come.
The extra 1775 shekalim, which became the hooks of the pillars, correspond to the rejected Jews of the tribe of Dan who stood outside the camp, and Haman's money did not counter their merit.
At the root of every Jewish soul, called Kol Yisrael, no sin can reach, and from there Hashem shows favor even to those who do not deserve it, as on Purim.
Parshas Parah, read after Purim, continues Purim: the red heifer is burned outside the camp and brings salvation to those who are outside.

sin of the Tree of Knowledge
Mordechai as repair of Adam's sin
Achashverosh's feast and the seventy years
rejected Jews of the tribe of Dan

title.en: Forty full days: Matan Torah as a mikveh

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks, from Rashi on the Golden Calf, why part of the first day could not count for Moshe's forty days. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar that a mikveh's forty se'ah are 960 lugin, the measure in which even a creature is nullified, so that the 960 hours of Elul to Yom Kippur are a mikveh, and applies this to Matan Torah, which needed 960 full hours.

title.en: The root of the mistake: not waiting

summary.en: The Mashgiach says every mistake has a root: the people did not wait one more day, just as Adam did not wait for Shabbos to make Kiddush from the Tree of Knowledge. Had they waited, Matan Torah would have brought the perfected world. He tells of the Malbim describing to the maskilim how a Jew must wait before he may eat, and concludes that the whole Torah is built on waiting.

title.en: Achashverosh's feast and Mordechai's repair

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the seventy years were miscalculated, and explains that the Jews went to Achashverosh's feast because they thought the redemption would no longer come, while Mordechai warned them to wait. Mordechai was thus a repair of Adam's sin, since the Tree of Knowledge mixed good and evil and waiting for Shabbos would have left only its good.

title.en: Our task now: waiting for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies the lesson: the repair of the sin is to wait for Moshiach. Though the signs in the Gemara fit this generation, one must not think the redemption has come; he calls the State of Israel a mixture of good and evil, and brings the navi's words about waiting for Hashem who hides His face.

title.en: The five final letters: din and geulah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings, from the Bnei Yissaschar in the name of the Arizal, that the five final letters are letters of din, the 280 judgments, and also, according to the Midrash, letters of redemption, each tied to a geulah from Avraham to the final one. He brings the passuk in Yeshayahu about awaiting the tzaddik and shows the five letters in Haman, Zeresh and his wise men.

title.en: Haman's shekalim and the forgotten Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Haman's ten thousand kikar matched the half-shekel of the 600,000, but not the extra 1775 shekalim that Moshe forgot and that became the hooks of the pillars. These correspond to the letters at the very end of the Torah and to the rejected Jews of the tribe of Dan, whom the cloud did not protect and Amalek attacked; Haman gave nothing against them, and they brought the salvation.

title.en: Tehillim 34 and the tribe of Dan

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that Tehillim 34, whose verse forms the letter combination of Dan's month, follows the whole aleph-beis and adds one last verse outside it, about Hashem redeeming His servants; this verse belongs to Dan's rejected ones and equals in gematria the hooks of the pillars. The whole aleph-beis with the five final letters totals 1775, the forgotten shekalim, showing they are included in Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Kol Yisrael: the root no sin reaches

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Hashem cares so much for the rejected of Dan, and answers from Parshas Ki Sisa, read near Purim: Hashem shows favor even to those who do not deserve it, looking to the root of the Jewish soul. He brings the Yismach Moshe on the 'island' of Kol Yisrael that no sin can blemish and the Rambam that every Jew inwardly wants Hashem's will, and ties this to the salvation of Purim and to 'ad delo yada'.

title.en: Parshas Parah: salvation outside the camp

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parshas Parah after Purim continues Purim and sweetens the 280 judgments. He brings the Tanya's question why the red heifer atones more than a chatas, and adds that the parah is done outside the camp, bringing salvation to those outside, like the last letters of the Torah. He closes with a brachah to be purified for Pesach.

catalogTitle: ב - ה' מנ"א תשל"ח - אמונה בתורת הסוד וביאור שנטמן האר"י הק' בימים אלו.
zman: מסיבת לחיים בקעמפ תורה ודעת דרשה אחר שריפה במחנה תורה ודעת (קעמפ)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that in a long galus Jews are judged by their emunah alone, and that the hidden light of the Nine Days, the days of the Arizal's passing, calls for believing in the secrets of the Torah even without understanding them.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach contrasts two nearly identical verses in Tehillim about Hashem coming to judge the world: if Moshiach comes early, Jews are judged by the measure of Torah; if galus drags on past kitz after kitz, they are judged by their emunah. Like watchmen waiting for morning, Jews keep hoping, and so Chavakuk based all the mitzvos on 'a tzaddik lives by his emunah'. On the Arizal's day of passing, he says the Arizal's words cannot be understood without ruach hakodesh, so at his tziyun one can only sing his zemiros. The Arizal and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai share one soul and passed away in days of mourning, whose light is too great for now and appears as darkness. Rabbi Shimon revealed open and hidden Torah, so his day is a joy; the Arizal's stays hidden. The Mashgiach ends by urging everyone to believe his emunah is whole.

en: The quality of Klal Yisrael is to keep waiting for the morning of the geulah, like watchmen, even after many kitzim and disappointments.
Chavakuk based all the mitzvos on emunah because his prophecy was for a generation that had fallen so low that emunah is what it can hold on to.
When the galus is long, Hashem judges the Jewish people by their emunah, not by the great Torah and avodah of earlier generations.
The Arizal's teachings cannot be understood without ruach hakodesh; at his tziyun one can at least sing his zemiros.
Days of mourning such as the Nine Days hide a light so great that it appears as darkness, kept for the tzaddikim in the future.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai revealed both the revealed and hidden Torah, so his day is joyous; the Arizal revealed only the hidden, so his day stays concealed.
Every Jew has a hidden point in his heart that believes in Hashem, and he should believe that his emunah is whole even when doubts arise.

candidateTopics: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the Arizal

title.en: Waiting for the morning: emunah in a long galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach points to two similar verses about Hashem coming to judge the world, and says Moshiach can come early or after a long wait. Like watchmen waiting for morning, Jews keep hoping after every kitz that passed, and this is why Chavakuk based all the mitzvos on emunah for a fallen generation.

title.en: Judged by uprightness or by emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a navi's name carries his message, and Chavakuk's is clinging to emunah. Had Moshiach come in earlier generations, each Jew would have been judged by his Torah and avodah; now, after the kitzim passed, the verse says the nations will be judged by their emunah.

title.en: The Arizal's day: singing at his tziyun

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that today is the Arizal's yahrzeit and that his secrets cannot be understood without ruach hakodesh. He tells how at the Arizal's tziyun in Tzfas, unable to say over his teaching, he sang his zemiros, and explains that the Arizal and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai are one soul who both passed away in days of mourning.

title.en: Hidden light, hidden secrets, and complete emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the days of sefirah and the Nine Days hold a light kept for the future, too great for us now, so it appears as darkness; Rabbi Shimon revealed both nigleh and nistar, so his day is a joy, while the Arizal revealed only secrets, so his day stays hidden. Returning to the verse, he calls on everyone to strengthen his emunah, believe in the secrets hidden in the Torah, and believe that his own emunah is whole.

catalogTitle: ג - ט"ו תמוז יארצייט האוה"ח הק' - תורה על הפרשה.
zman: מסיבת לחיים בקעמפ תורה ודעת דרשה אחר שריפה במחנה תורה ודעת (קעמפ)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach asks how Bilaam's impure mouth could speak the holy blessings and prophecies of the days of Moshiach, and begins to explain it through the Gemara and the Ba'al Shem Tov's reading of Bilaam's blind eye.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the passuk that Hashem put a word in Bilaam's mouth. Bilaam had an impure mouth, yet he spoke the holy parshiyos of Bilaam: the great blessings and the prophecies about the days of Moshiach. How could such a mouth say such things? The Mashgiach explains that Hashem put something into his mouth that served as a barrier, so that the words would not come from Bilaam's own mouth. He brings the Gemara that Hashem placed a hook in his mouth, so that the words came out from that foreign thing and not from Bilaam's mouth. He then turns to the words 'shesum ha'ayin': Rashi explains that Bilaam's eye was blinded, while the Targum explains that he saw clearly, two opposite readings. The Ba'al Shem Tov reconciles them: Hashem made one of Bilaam's eyes blind so that he could not harm with it.

en: The Mashgiach asks how Bilaam, with his impure mouth, could speak the holy blessings and the prophecies of the days of Moshiach.
Hashem placed something in Bilaam's mouth as a barrier, so that the holy words came out of that foreign thing and not from his own mouth.
The Ba'al Shem Tov explains that Bilaam had one blind eye, made so by Hashem so that he could not do harm with it, which bridges Rashi's and the Targum's opposite readings of 'shesum ha'ayin'.

title.en: Holy words from Bilaam's impure mouth

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how Bilaam's impure mouth could speak holy blessings and prophecies, answers from the Gemara that Hashem put a hook in his mouth as a barrier, and brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on Rashi's and the Targum's opposite readings of Bilaam's eye.

catalogTitle: בבית המדרש אמונת ישראל

oneLiner.en: At a l'chaim for the Ohr HaChaim, the Mashgiach explains that the Ohr HaChaim is a reflection of Moshiach, and reads his remez on the passuk 'ki yihyeh vecha evyon' as describing Moshiach's longing for Klal Yisrael.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the tradition that the Ba'al Shem Tov, who had the nefesh of Moshiach, wished to meet the Ohr HaChaim, who had the ruach of Moshiach, and that their meeting would have brought the redemption, but it was held back from Heaven. He connects the Ohr HaChaim to the days around the Seventeenth of Tammuz, the day Moshe brought down the first luchos, a day that keeps a great power because in the world of tikkun every lost virtue returns. He then reads the Ohr HaChaim's remez on 'ki yihyeh vecha evyon' in parshas Re'eh: the evyon is Moshiach, who longs for Klal Yisrael and wept on hearing that Jews await him; the passuk asks a Jew not to harden his heart, to share in Moshiach's longing, and to do every mitzvah with the intent of bringing him. He closes with three stories of the Ohr HaChaim.

en: The Mashgiach explains that the Ohr HaChaim is a reflection of Moshiach: the Ba'al Shem Tov said he himself had the nefesh of Moshiach and the Ohr HaChaim its ruach.
The Seventeenth of Tammuz, the day Moshe was to bring down the first luchos, still holds a great power, since in the world of tikkun every lost virtue returns.
Following the Ohr HaChaim, the 'evyon' of the passuk in Re'eh is Moshiach, who longs for Klal Yisrael like a pauper longs for what he lacks.
Not hardening one's heart means sharing in Moshiach's longing and having compassion on him.
With every good deed, whether tefillah, tefillin or a page of Gemara, a Jew should have in mind that he does it to bring Moshiach.
