the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Ohr HaChaim
Deuteronomy 15:7 as a remez to Moshiach
having Moshiach in mind with every mitzvah

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim and the Seventeenth of Tammuz

summary.en: After a l'chaim, the Mashgiach brings the tradition that the Ba'al Shem Tov wished to meet the Ohr HaChaim, since together they held the nefesh and ruach of Moshiach. He then explains that the Seventeenth of Tammuz, the day of the first luchos, keeps a great power for the future tikkun, and that the words of the Ohr HaChaim can bring great awakenings.

title.en: Moshiach as the evyon of parshas Re'eh

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the passuk 'ki yihyeh vecha evyon' with the Ohr HaChaim's remez that the evyon is Moshiach. He explains the name evyon as one who longs for what he lacks, brings Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's encounter in which Moshiach wept on hearing that Jews await him, and reads 'one of your gates' as Moshiach being the unique one of the Sanhedrin.

title.en: Teshuvah, a soft heart and every mitzvah for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a second reading: Chazal say that if one congregation does teshuvah Moshiach comes at once, and he explains that the teshuvah asked of each generation differs. From 'do not harden your heart' he explains that a Jew must feel compassion and share in Moshiach's longing, and with every mitzvah have in mind to bring Moshiach.

title.en: Stories of the Ohr HaChaim

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells three stories: the Ohr HaChaim finding a Rambam hidden under a step in the Karaite synagogue in Yerushalayim, the lion that guarded him in the desert over Shabbos, and the Chida's account of Eliyahu HaNavi visiting him. He closes by saying that honoring the Ohr HaChaim, a reflection of Moshiach, should bring a strong longing for Moshiach.

catalogTitle: An Explanation of Excerpts from the קדושת לוי - ספרים and יסוד יוסף

oneLiner.en: Reading inside the Kedushas Levi and the Yesod Yosef, the Mashgiach explains that on Purim a new, heavenly light comes down into the natural world through the Megillah, through tzedakah and through the seudah, and that a person should receive it with preparation and simcha, not with drunkenness.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach continues from the previous week to give a sense of what Purim is, reading pieces of the Yesod Yosef and the Kedushas Levi inside so that the holy words reach the neshamah. Every Purim a new 'olam', a hidden world, comes down and stays ever new; it begins with the reading of the Megillah, a revealing of what was hidden. Purim is 'reishis', above the seven middos of this world, which is why Haman of Amalek, the reishis of tumah, fought Mordechai. Unlike Yom Kippur, when we rise to heaven, on Purim heaven descends into nature: the Megillah's miracles look natural, the names of Hashem hide in its words, and its reading purifies even the physical. The Mashgiach then speaks of preparing for the Megillah as a fresh start, of the special power of tzedakah on Purim, and closes by urging simcha without drunkenness, citing the Gemara, the Rema and a tzaddik whose 'drunkenness' came from the Megillah itself.

en: Every Purim a new, hidden 'olam' comes down to this world, and by its nature it stays new each year.
This light begins to come down with the reading of the Megillah, which reveals what was hidden, so one should answer amen to the brachah with great kavanah.
On Yom Kippur we rise up to heaven; on Purim heaven comes down into food, drink and the natural world.
The reading of the Megillah purifies even the physical world and the gashmiyus of whoever reads or hears it.
Tzedakah given on Purim is far more powerful than tzedakah during the year, and its flow of blessing reaches all the way down into this world.
The Mashgiach urges simcha on Purim without becoming drunk; the Megillah itself should be what makes a person 'drunk'.

candidateTopics: hidden names of Hashem in the Megillah

title.en: Purim beyond our grasp; reading the sefarim inside

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is so sublime that the conscious mind cannot hold it, comparing it to pain beyond tolerance that needs an anesthetic. He introduces the Yesod Yosef, a kabbalistic sefer, and the Kedushas Levi, and explains why he will read them inside: written holy words pierce through gashmiyus into the neshamah.

title.en: A new world revealed through the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains 'olam' as something concealed, and says that on Purim a new olam comes down that stays new every year. It starts to come down with the reading of the Megillah, a 'revealing' of what was hidden, so one should answer amen to the brachah with great kavanah and stand ready to receive it.

title.en: Heaven on earth: Purim as reishis

summary.en: After noting that the Maharal hides kabbalah in plain words, the Mashgiach begins the Kedushas Levi: Purim brings 'days of heaven upon earth'. Purim is reishis, above the seven middos on which this world runs; Amalek is the reishis of tumah, and Haman sought the fiftieth level of tumah against Mordechai.

title.en: Purim and Yom Kippur; the obligation of the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares Purim to Yom Kippur: on Yom Kippur we rise to heaven like malachim, on Purim heaven comes down into food and drink, so Purim is no 'Jewish Halloween'. From this he explains the Kedushas Levi's point that the obligation to hear the Megillah is stronger than that of Krias HaTorah, and likewise Parshas Zachor.

title.en: Hidden names and natural miracles

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the names of Hashem are hidden in the Megillah at its turning points, and its miracles all look like natural events. He tells how the Chiddushei HaRim pictured a man bringing news of Vashti into a beis medrash and being told to stop, not knowing it would become the Megillah. Then he reads the Kedushas Levi that through the Megillah the vitality of the spiritual comes down to be tasted in the natural world.

title.en: The Megillah purifies the physical

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the Megillah is read from a written scroll of parchment and ink: all of nature becomes purified, and the names in it light up in whoever reads or hears it and purify his gashmiyus. Unlike at Sinai, when the physical resisted the Torah, the Megillah purifies matter itself; a person should prepare for it by leaving the past behind.

title.en: A new beginning; this year's deeper descent

summary.en: Like Yom Kippur, the Megillah is a fresh start, and the Kedushas Levi writes that with every word a new light and a new malach come about. The Mashgiach adds that this year the Megillah's light must come down deeper than ever because the world has sunk lower, so wherever a person is, he should welcome it.

title.en: The special power of tzedakah on Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tzedakah on Purim, matanos la'evyonim, is charged with far more power than all year: as a shadow mimics a person, Hashem gives to us as we give, and on Purim the shefa does not get stuck but reaches this world. He brings the Kedushas Levi's blessing that one who gives on Purim receives a thousandfold, and urges giving with simcha, personally, and training children to give.

title.en: Simcha without drunkenness

summary.en: Reading the Kedushas Levi's last paragraph against foolishness, the Mashgiach discusses drinking on Purim: the Gemara's 'ad delo yada', the story of Rabbah and Rav Zeira, the Rishonim's dispute and the Rema's 'a little more than usual'. He urges not becoming drunk, telling of a tzaddik who became 'drunk' from the Megillah itself, and closes with wishes for Shabbos and the geulah.

catalogTitle: א - ביאור המדרש על הפס' “קראתי למאהבי המה רמוני'” זמן לעבוד ה' באבילות.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the Midrash that the prophets 'deceived' Klal Yisrael to keep their hope for Moshiach alive, and teaches that in the days of mourning the way to Yerushalayim and to Heaven is through tears, broken hearts and the prayer Moshe Rabbeinu left unfinished.

abstract.en: Drawing on the Yaaros Devash, the Mashgiach brings the Midrash on 'I called to my lovers, they deceived me': the prophets instituted terumah and maaser outside Eretz Yisrael so that Jews would believe Moshiach is near. Since the end was hidden lest Jews despair, this 'deception' kept hope alive, and that hope after two thousand years is itself a sign of redemption. He explains Yerushalayim as yirah and shalom, the place of the Shechinah to which every Jewish soul is drawn, and says that in these days the passport to Heaven is weeping, not joy. Through a question of the Avnei Nezer on R' Yochanan he shows that Hashem Himself burned the Beis HaMikdash, renewed each moment, and that warm tefillos and tears will rebuild it. He ends with Vaeschanan: Moshe's prayers lacked one more, which Klal Yisrael must complete on Tisha B'Av.

en: The Mashgiach brings that the end of the exile was hidden so that Jews would not fall into despair over how long it would take.
Every Jew's soul comes from the Kisei HaKavod and is naturally drawn to Yerushalayim, so in the time of churban he naturally feels its absence.
Hashem fills a lack according to how much it is felt, so the more Klal Yisrael feels the absence of Yerushalayim, the more it hastens its rebuilding.
Tisha B'Av is the 'end of days' of the year, its lowest point, when a pure heart can hear the Shechinah weeping over Yerushalayim.
Yerushalayim is being built now, year after year, from stones made of broken Jewish hearts and tears.
Citing the Chasam Sofer, the Mashgiach says every year without the Beis HaMikdash is a new churban, as the world sinks lower and foreign influences break through the walls.
Every Tisha B'Av is a new battle for Yerushalayim, and every Jew must be a soldier whose weapons are the kinos, the weeping and the mourning.

candidateTopics: Moshe Rabbeinu's prayer to enter Eretz Yisrael

title.en: The Midrash: 'they deceived me'

summary.en: The Mashgiach draws on the Yaaros Devash, which brings the Midrash that the 'lovers' who 'deceived' Klal Yisrael are the prophets who instituted terumah and maaser outside Eretz Yisrael. He asks what deception this was, and brings that the end of the exile was hidden so that Jews would not despair over its length.

title.en: Why the prophets kept hope alive

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a takanah meant to last two thousand years would make little sense; the prophets made it so Jews would feel Moshiach is near. He speaks of the many disappointed hopes over the kitzim and says that the Jews' hope after two thousand years is itself a sign they must be redeemed.

title.en: What Yerushalayim is

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Yerushalayim as the city of G-dliness, a piece of heaven on earth and the place where the Shechinah rests, made of yirah and shalom like Shabbos. Every Jew whose soul comes from the Kisei HaKavod is drawn to it, like the strings of Dovid HaMelech's harp.

title.en: Feeling the lack of Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that mourning in these days is the natural feeling of a Jew that Yerushalayim is missing, and that Hashem fills a lack as much as it is felt. He brings the Chasam Sofer on the Yerushalmi about the earlier and later generations, explaining with the parable of a man who knows his heart is weak and does nothing.

title.en: Weeping: the passport to Heaven now

summary.en: Usually simcha is the passport to Heaven, since 'strength and joy are in His place'. But in these days Hashem has called for weeping and mourning, the angels cry and the King of the Midrash puts out the lamps, so the Mashgiach says one reaches Heaven now only through weeping, sharing the Shechinah's sorrow.

title.en: End of days; building with broken hearts

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer that 'the end of days' in Devarim is Tisha B'Av, the lowest point of the year, when a cleansed heart can hear the Shechinah weeping. Jews must not be silent, and 'Boneh Yerushalayim Hashem' means Yerushalayim is being built now from broken hearts, which Hashem will heal into joy.

title.en: R' Yitzchak Nafcha pleases both students

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara where R' Ami and R' Assi sat before R' Yitzchak Nafcha, one wanting halachah and the other agadah. He told them a teaching on fire, 'I lit a fire in Zion', together with the halachah of damage by fire, and the Mashgiach asks how this satisfied both.

title.en: The Avnei Nezer's question on R' Yochanan

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Avnei Nezer: R' Yochanan said he would have fixed the fast on the tenth of Av, when most of the burning happened, yet he also holds 'isho mishum chitzav', which by the Nimukei Yosef attributes a fire to its start. He begins his answer with two modes of Divine conduct, knowledge and free choice, and why a murderer cannot plead that Hashem runs the world.

title.en: Hashem burned it, moment by moment

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that the Beis HaMikdash was above time and place, so Hashem, not Titus, burned it; and since Hashem creates everything anew each moment (Nefesh HaChaim), each moment of the burning was a new fire, which fits R' Yochanan and reconciles the agadah and the halachah for his students R' Ami and R' Assi. The fire that burned Zion was the sins; the fire that will rebuild it is the warmth of Jewish tefillos and tears.

title.en: Vaeschanan: praying in a time of distress

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Tisha B'Av always comes with parshas Vaeschanan, and each reading awakens its time. He explains that one cannot always daven, and brings the Yalkut that Moshe's prayer teaches all generations to pray in distress; his distress was that he could not enter Eretz Yisrael and see Yerushalayim and the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: A new churban each year; Tisha B'Av as battle

summary.en: Citing the Chasam Sofer, the Mashgiach says each year is a new churban, describing how the culture of the street, Hollywood and the universities breaks into the beis medrash. Tisha B'Av, like crying out in time of war, is a battle in which every Jew must be a soldier, fighting with kinos and mourning.

title.en: Moshe's one missing prayer

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why this was Moshe's worst distress, and answers that like R' Chanina ben Dosa he could sense his prayer was not accepted, yet pushed to break through. His 515 prayers were in truth accepted but lacked one more, which Klal Yisrael must complete through the generations, especially when Tisha B'Av meets Vaeschanan, since we are now in history's 'end of days'.

catalogTitle: ב - מוצאי ט' באב - מעשה רבי ר' אלימלך

oneLiner.en: Through the story of a disciple of Rebbe Reb Elimelech stranded on an island, the Mashgiach teaches that wherever a Jew finds himself is a mission from Heaven.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach tells a story, related by the Alexander Rebbe, about one of the yoshvim who sat and learned in Rebbe Reb Elimelech's beis medrash and received a weekly stipend. When his envelope began to shrink and then came empty, he understood it as a sign that he was no longer worthy, and after teshuvah and fasts did not help, his friends collected money and sent him overseas to trade. On the way home the ship left him behind on an island. Near death from thirst he found a little water, yet remembered he was a talmid of Rebbe Reb Elimelech and made a shehakol and a borei nefashos with great kavanah. Back in Lizhensk, the Rebbe told him two souls had waited on that island for hundreds of years for exactly those brachos. The Mashgiach concludes that every place a person reaches is a shlichus, adds a second short story about a bracha on a drink, and says a Jew must never despair but use every moment there.

en: The disciple took his shrinking stipend as a sign from Rebbe Reb Elimelech that he was no longer worthy, and tried to correct himself with teshuvah and fasting.
Even near death from thirst, he held back and made a bracha with great kavanah before drinking, because he was a talmid of Rebbe Reb Elimelech.
Rebbe Reb Elimelech revealed that two souls had waited on that island for hundreds of years and were brought to their tikkun through his brachos.
The Mashgiach teaches that everything a person does in a given place, which tree he learns under and which water he drinks, is a mission sent from Heaven.
A Jew must never despair; wherever he arrives he should use every moment for Torah, tefillah and chessed, knowing he is Hashem's messenger.

candidateTopics: every place as a mission from Heaven

title.en: The disciple whose stipend shrank

summary.en: The Mashgiach begins a story told by the Alexander Rebbe about the yoshvim in Rebbe Reb Elimelech's beis medrash, who got weekly money from the gabbai. One of them found less and less in his envelope and finally nothing; taking it as a sign that he was no longer worthy, he did teshuvah and fasted.

title.en: Sent overseas and left on an island

summary.en: He asks his friends for advice, and they collect money and send him overseas to trade. On the way back the ship stops at an island; absorbed in Tehillim under a tree he misses the ship's whistle and is left behind alone.

title.en: Thirst, and a brachah with kavanah

summary.en: Near death from thirst, he finds a little water; though a man in such a state becomes like an animal, he remembers he is a talmid of Rebbe Reb Elimelech and makes a shehakol and borei nefashos with great kavanah. When the ship returns he goes home to Lizhensk, and the Rebbe begins to tell him about two souls on the island.

title.en: The souls' tikkun; every place is a mission

summary.en: Rebbe Reb Elimelech explains that his brachos brought the souls to their tikkun and that he arranged the causes to send him there. The Mashgiach draws from the passuk of a man's steps being set by Hashem that everything a person does is a shlichus, adds a short story about brandy drunk without a bracha, and concludes that a Jew must never despair but use every moment wherever he is sent.

catalogTitle: בענין התהפכות ירמיהו הנביא לשלמה המלך וט' באב לשמיני עצרת

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Yirmiyahu, the prophet of the churban, is a gilgul of Shlomo HaMelech, and that Tisha B'Av, the day of Yirmiyahu, will one day turn into Shemini Atzeres, the day of Shlomo.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Shemini Atzeres, the center of all the yomim tovim, and its haftorah, which says Shlomo HaMelech completed all he desired. No person achieves that, he says, but Shlomo, who ruled the world through wisdom and peace, brought down a model of the days of Moshiach. His era was the complete union of Hashem and Klal Yisroel, and Shemini Atzeres is his day. Tisha B'Av is its opposite, the day of the 'divorce', and Yirmiyahu is its soul. Citing the Chasam Sofer and the mekubalim, he explains that Yirmiyahu is a gilgul of Shlomo, sent back to see the destruction of the Temple he built. Therefore Tisha B'Av will become Shemini Atzeres. He shows this in the seudah hamafsekes on a Shabbos erev Tisha B'Av, the Pinchas maftir, the end of Masechta Taanis and the word 'moed' in Eicha, and calls on everyone, especially broken bochurim, to feel what is missing and bring Moshiach.

en: Shemini Atzeres is the center around which all the yomim tovim revolve, and it is the day of Shlomo HaMelech.
Shlomo ruled the whole world through wisdom and peace, without war, and his era was a model of the days of Moshiach.
Shlomo's time was the complete union of Hashem and Klal Yisroel, while Tisha B'Av is the day of separation, with Yirmiyahu as its soul.
Yirmiyahu is a gilgul of Shlomo, sent back to see the destruction of the Beis Hamikdash he himself built.
Since time and soul correspond, Tisha B'Av is a gilgul of Shemini Atzeres and will become the greatest yom tov.
On a Shabbos erev Tisha B'Av the seudah hamafsekes is eaten like the feast of Shlomo in his time, and Shlomo rather than Yirmiyahu is the guest.
The Mashgiach says the small, lowly last generations will bring Moshiach, when they feel what is missing and add Torah, tefillah and guarding themselves.

candidateTopics: Tisha B'Av turning into a yom tov

title.en: Shemini Atzeres and Shlomo's completed desire

summary.en: After thanking Rav Twersky, the Mashgiach describes Shemini Atzeres as the center of all the yomim tovim and the day of Shlomo HaMelech, and brings its haftorah that Shlomo completed all he desired. He asks how that can be, when no person achieves everything and the Midrash says Hashem Himself has not yet rejoiced in His works.

title.en: Shlomo's kingdom as a model of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that Shlomo became king of the world without war, through wisdom alone, as in the judgment of the two women, and his reign brought peace and abundance. Comparing it to the Rambam's description of the days of Moshiach, he concludes that Shlomo lifted his generation above the limits of time into a taste of Moshiach's days, when every desire can be fulfilled.

title.en: The full moon and Shlomo as soul of the union

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shlomo's era was the complete union of Hashem and Klal Yisroel, and that Tisha B'Av is its opposite, a 'divorce'. He brings the Midrash that the fifteen generations from Avraham to Shlomo parallel the waxing moon, which waned until Tzidkiyahu, and, using Sefer Yetzirah's parallel of time and soul, calls Shlomo, the author of Shir Hashirim, the soul of the union.

title.en: Yirmiyahu, the soul of Tisha B'Av

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Yirmiyahu the soul of Tisha B'Av: he cursed his birth and told Hashem He had persuaded him to become a prophet, yet he became the prophet of the churban. He brings the Midrash of the kohen who had to deal with a sotah who was his own mother, and applies it to Tziyon, the mother of Klal Yisroel, concluding that Shlomo and Yirmiyahu stand at opposite ends.

title.en: Yirmiyahu as a gilgul of Shlomo

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer, citing the mekubalim, that Yirmiyahu is a gilgul of Shlomo. Through the Gemara that Rome began to rise on the day Shlomo married Pharaoh's daughter, and Rashi's rule that Yerushalayim and Rome rise at each other's expense, he explains that the churban was decreed then, together with Shlomo's return as Yirmiyahu to witness it.

title.en: Tisha B'Av will become Shemini Atzeres

summary.en: Since Yirmiyahu is a gilgul of Shlomo, the Mashgiach says, Tisha B'Av is a gilgul of Shemini Atzeres and will become the greatest yom tov; its mourning clothes will be exchanged for Shlomo's royal garments, Eicha will turn back into Shir Hashirim, and the fasts will become days of joy. He brings the Rebbe of Lublin's word, and the story of a tzaddik who on Tisha B'Av showed with tears how kiddush will be made on that day.

title.en: The special food of each yom tov

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every major yom tov has its own food, like matzah on Pesach, so that the yom tov becomes part of a Jew's body and stays with him afterwards. Tisha B'Av also must be taken in, and for this Chazal instituted the seudah hamafsekes, which is itself part of Tisha B'Av.

title.en: This year's seudah: Shlomo as the guest

summary.en: At the seudah hamafsekes, the Mashgiach says, Yirmiyahu comes as a guest with his Eicha. This year, when Tisha B'Av falls after Shabbos, a rare order of readings and haftoros, the Mashgiach says, makes it a year of consolation, and Shlomo himself will sit at the table singing zemiros, as the Shulchan Aruch says one eats on such a Shabbos like the feast of Shlomo in his time.

title.en: Feeling the loss and adding one's share

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls this a great kindness and a call to arousal, bringing the Rebbe of Lublin that the three Shabbosos of the three weeks parallel the three regalim, with Shemini Atzeres as the fourth. With a story of a 'hole in the pocket' he urges that the days before Shabbos be used to feel the loss of the Beis Hamikdash, add Torah, tzedakah and tefillah, and ask for malchus shamayim, malchus beis Dovid and the Beis Hamikdash.

title.en: Pinchas, the end of Taanis, and Shlomo's crown

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that in an ordinary year the maftir of Pinchas, about Shemini Atzeres, is followed at once by Divrei Yirmiyahu, joining the two. He then brings the end of Masechta Taanis, which closes on the day of Shlomo's wedding, and explains that Tisha B'Av only looks like a bill of divorce; Hashem tells the daughters of Tziyon to look at King Shlomo with the crown that will be placed on Moshiach.

title.en: The laughter of Moshiach and the small generations

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the laughter of 'then our mouths will be filled with laughter': the Ba'al Shem Tov, the Maggid, Rebbe Reb Elimelech and the Chozeh of Lublin tried to bring Moshiach and could not, and the lowly last generations will bring him. He calls on the yeshiva bochurim to feel that something is missing, not to say nothing is lacking, and stresses the worth of a young man today who learns, davens and guards himself amid all the tests.

title.en: Tisha B'Av, the hidden moed, and fallen bochurim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Maggid of Mezritch on souls that are like Shabbos, and the Rokeach's finding of all the yomim tovim in the parshiyos. One yom tov is not written there: Tisha B'Av, which is called a moed and has no tachanun. He compares it to a bochur with talents who fell through bad friends; he is a moed that fell, and he can catch himself and return.

title.en: Eicha turned to joy, and the closing blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach says this Shabbos leading into Tisha B'Av is a special time for broken bochurim, as Yirmiyahu becomes Shlomo and Tisha B'Av becomes Shemini Atzeres. He brings remazim on Eicha and on the 'bill of divorce', mentions that the Berditchever saw the third Beis Hamikdash every Shabbos Chazon, and closes with the blessing that through Torah, tefillah and good middos the fasts will become days of joy, as Zechariah promised.

catalogTitle: המן- The Architect of his Own Demise

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach shows that in the Megillah, where Hashem hides His face, Haman himself prepared every step of his own downfall, and that Amalek's attack on 'the end' fails because the Jewish people have no end.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the twelve months, which correspond to the twelve tribes arranged in four camps. Nisan, the month of Yehuda and of the miracles of Egypt, comes first; the months descend until Adar, the last, whose Megillah has no open miracle at all. This is hester panim: Hashem hides, yet controls everything, and every small story in the Megillah is a wheel in one mechanism. The Mashgiach reads Chazal's identification of Memuchan with Haman as a signal to watch Haman, who unknowingly prepared Esther's rise, Mordechai's honor, his house and his own gallows. Adar means a cloak, and Dan is the last and most removed tribe, yet his son Chushim killed Esav. Amalek attacks those at the end, outside the camp, as Haman rejoiced when the lot fell on Adar; but the Jewish people have no end, and Purim protects those at the end.

en: The months descend from Nisan, named for its miracles, to Adar, whose Megillah contains no open miracle at all.
The message of the Megillah is that even when no miracles are seen, Hashem is hidden but controls everything.
Haman prepared every element of his own downfall: Vashti's removal, Mordechai's honor, his house and the gallows.
Dan, the last tribe, is the most removed from holiness and always gets into trouble, yet he remains connected to the Shem Havayah.
Amalek attacks those at the end, outside the camp, and Haman likewise hoped to prevail in Adar, the month of the end.
The Jewish people have no end: Amalek has an end, but when the Jews finish they begin again.

candidateTopics: leadership in the generation before Moshiach

title.en: Twelve months, twelve tribes, and Adar

summary.en: The Mashgiach matches the twelve months to the twelve tribes in their four camps, from Nisan and Yehuda to Adar at the end. He notes that Amalek has no future, and that the months descend from Nisan's miracles to Adar's Megillah, where no open miracle appears.

title.en: Hidden face: Haman prepares everything

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara's source for Esther in the Torah, hester panim, and explains that every small story in the Megillah is a wheel in one mechanism. From Chazal's identification of Memuchan with Haman he shows that Haman prepared Vashti's removal, Mordechai's greatness and his own gallows.

title.en: Only Haman knew how to do it

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls it a mockery of avodah zarah that it prepares its own demise. Mordechai, a tzaddik with rachmanus and no taste for honor, could not have devised the cruel gallows, the royal honor or the mansion; Haman did all three, unknowingly for Mordechai.

title.en: Adar the cloak; Dan and Chushim

summary.en: Returning to the months, the Mashgiach explains that Adar means a cloak, as with Esav's mantle of hair: the miracles are covered. Dan, the last and most removed tribe, still bears a permutation of the Shem Havayah, and it was Dan's son Chushim, deaf and mute, who killed Esav at Yaakov's burial.

title.en: The last generation: hester panim today

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls the generation before Moshiach a generation of Chushim and of great hester panim. He recalls that in his youth there were universally accepted leaders, the last being the Chazon Ish, while today great men are accepted only by their own factions.

title.en: Amalek attacks the end; Adar Sheini

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that those of Dan expelled from the camp were outside the Clouds of Glory, so Amalek could strike the stragglers. Haman, like Amalek, rejoiced when the lot fell on Adar, the month of the end, and a leap year's Adar Sheini, likened to the last eight pesukim of the Torah, seemed even more outside the camp. His mistake: these too belong to the camp.

title.en: No end for Yidden; Shushan Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that the Jews have no end: when they finish the Torah they begin Bereishis again, and Purim protects those at the end of the camp. He then speaks of the special holiness of Shushan Purim, kept today only in Yerushalayim, and of his plan to be there.

catalogTitle: צריכים להרגיש יותר הצער של שריפת בית אלוקינו; ולהיות מובדל מפגמים דקים

oneLiner.en: Taking the fire that broke out the day before as a message from Hashem, the Mashgiach calls for feeling the burning of the Beis HaMikdash more deeply and for 'making havdalah' again and again, separating oneself even from fine flaws.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Rambam that crying out to Hashem in every trouble is a path of teshuvah, and that calling a trouble chance is cruelty. Every passuk speaks to every generation, and this week's 'a people heard the voice of G-d speaking from the fire' speaks to the fire that broke out in the camp the day before. He tells how the kabbalists of Jerusalem brought about the takanah against music at Jerusalem weddings, because the churban is felt more there; the Nine Days are such a time, and one must feel the burning of the Beis HaMikdash. A mashal of the king's violinist shows why Torah study is so precious, and the fire disrupted learning. He then explains the segulah of relighting the havdalah candle: fire does not distinguish, so one who keeps distinguishing more finely is saved from fire. He applies this to refinement in Shabbos, tefillah and going beyond the letter of the law, and closes with gratitude for the miracles and the promise of consolation.

en: Following the Rambam, the Mashgiach teaches that troubles are signals from Heaven; calling them chance is cruelty that brings more troubles.
The fire in the camp is Hashem speaking 'from within the fire', and a person with sense must understand one thing from another.

There are places and times, Jerusalem and the Nine Days, where the churban must be felt more, and the Mashgiach says each person according to his level should feel the burning of the Beis HaMikdash more.
Fire does not distinguish, so the remedy for fire is havdalah: making ever finer distinctions, as with a torch rather than a small candle.
A refined Jew does not settle for fulfilling his obligation; he goes beyond the letter of the law and responds to Hashem's hints.
One should become 'rich' from the fire in Torah, yiras shamayim and fine observance, and thank Hashem for the miracles that came with it.

title.en: The Rambam: troubles are not chance

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the opening of the Rambam's Hilchos Taaniyos: crying out in trouble is a path of teshuvah, and calling it chance is cruelty. He applies this week's passuk 'speaking from within the fire' to the fire in the camp the day before, a signal not to be taken lightly.

title.en: No music at Jerusalem weddings

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how, during an epidemic in Jerusalem, Rabbi Meir Auerbach learned through a she'elas chalom that the Kosel is where mourning for Jerusalem must be greater, and how the rabbanim enacted that no instruments be played at weddings in Jerusalem. A wealthy man who defied the takanah suffered a frightening punishment.

title.en: Feeling the burning of the Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: Just as there is a place, there is a time when the churban is felt more: the Nine Days. The Mashgiach rebukes himself and the camp for carrying on as usual, asks them to picture the fire on Har HaBayis, and reads the repeated small fires as a reminder from Heaven, calling for 'let us search our ways'.

title.en: The king's violinist and bitul Torah

summary.en: On 'for what was the land lost... because they forsook My Torah' the Mashgiach brings a mashal of a king who ignored his violinist's crimes until he could no longer play. Torah study is what would bring the other sins to be repaired; since the fire disrupted the learning in the camp, it is a call to strengthen Torah.

title.en: Havdalah again: a segulah against fire

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the custom of relighting the havdalah candle as a segulah against fire. Havdalah requires da'as; a coarse person distinguishes only gross differences, as by a small candle, while a refined Jew uses a torch to see fine ones. Fire does not distinguish, so one who keeps making havdalah is saved from fire, measure for measure.

title.en: Refinement beyond the obligation

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks each one to demand more of himself: even the weekday brachos of Shemoneh Esreh should feel different on Shabbos, as shown by the ger tzedek who asked the Vilna Gaon how one could not recognize Shabbos in the desert. Citing the Mesillas Yesharim and the example of tevilah, he explains that serving from love means following hints, and that Jerusalem was destroyed because they kept to the letter of the law.

title.en: Each Jew is a Jerusalem

summary.en: Wherever there is yiras shamayim there is Jerusalem, so each Jew must rebuild the Mikdash in his heart and go beyond the letter of the law. A fire that does not distinguish came because they did not; the fire in the camp asks for more havdalah, with great da'as, again and again, and for seeing everything as hashgachah pratis.

title.en: Becoming rich after the fire; thanks and consolation

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks that the fire make everyone richer in yiras shamayim and Torah. He contrasts the enemies who ran to defile the sifrei Torah with the bochurim who ran to save them, thanks Hashem for the miracles, and closes with Hashem's promise to rebuild Zion with fire and console doubly.

catalogTitle: דרוש נפלא בענין ט' באב שחל בשבת וטובת הגלות' והאיך הגלות מושרש בגאולה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach shows that the exile of Av is rooted in the redemption of Nissan, that the hidden sparks and forgotten souls of the exile are the seeds of Moshiach, and that on Shabbos Nachamu one must accept the prophet's consolation with emunah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with 'Nachamu nachamu ami' after yet another Tisha B'Av and asks what 'ki mal'ah tzva'ah' means. He describes the yearly cycle of rising and falling, with Tammuz and Av given to Esav. From the rare trop 'yerach ben yomo', found only in Masei and serving the 'karnei parah' that is sung like a 'pazer', he builds his theme: following the Maharal, exile is rooted in redemption. Av, the month of Shimon and the lion, draws its blessing from Nissan, the month of Yehudah, whose every day is fresh like 'ben yomo'. The divided cow's horn of Av becomes the shofar of Moshiach. Yaakov's gift to Esav and the gid hanasheh stand for forgotten souls that will return; Dinah in Shechem held the spark of Moshiach ben Yosef. Exile is a mission to gather sparks. He ends with emunah in the redemption, the seven weeks of consolation, Tu B'Av, and receiving Yeshaya's good tidings.

en: Following the Maharal, every exile is rooted in redemption, and the purpose of exile is the geulah.
Av, the month of Shimon, receives its blessing from Nissan, the month of Yehudah, just as Shimon was blessed and given his inheritance within Yehudah's.
The 'karnei parah' of Av stands for division and exile, but joined with the 'yerach ben yomo' of Nissan it becomes the shofar of Moshiach.
Yaakov's gift to Esav and the gid hanasheh represent forgotten Jewish souls that fell under Esav, and they must all return.
The exile is not only a punishment but a mission from Hashem to gather the sparks scattered among the nations.
Although another Tisha B'Av has passed, one may not lose emunah; Moshiach will not delay once everything is complete.

title.en: Nachamu after another Tisha B'Av; the cycle of the year

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Hashem's command to the prophet to comfort His people after yet another Tisha B'Av, and asks what 'ki mal'ah tzva'ah' means. He describes the yearly cycle of rising and falling, with Teves, Tammuz and Av given to Esav, down to Tisha B'Av and up again from the fifteenth of Av.

title.en: The rare trop 'yerach ben yomo' in Masei

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the only 'yerach ben yomo' in the Torah appears in Masei, serving the 'karnei parah', which the Masorah says is sung like a 'pazer', and asks why it is needed and why it falls on the first Shabbos of Av. He brings the Midrash that the first day of Pesach and Tisha B'Av fall on the same day of the week.

title.en: Exile rooted in redemption: Av and Nissan

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Maharal that exile is rooted in redemption, with Yocheved born as the Egyptian exile began and Moshiach born on Tisha B'Av. Through the Bnei Yissaschar he shows that Av, the month of Shimon, draws its blessing from Nissan, the month of Yehudah, and that the lion of Av hides chesed beneath gevurah.

title.en: The seven 'pazers' and the cow's horn

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the descent begins in Sivan, when Behaaloscha with its seven 'pazers' is read, and that 'pazer', scattering, is exile whose inner side is redemption. From the Mishnah that a cow's horn is unfit for a shofar, since it is made of layers, he explains that the shofar means unity and the ingathering, while the 'karnei parah' means division, the cause of the exile.

title.en: Nissan: every day a new Rosh Chodesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Shelah that every day of Nissan has the holiness of Rosh Chodesh, and explains it through the halachic idea of 'ben yomo', something still fresh from the same day. Nissan, the month of freshness, serves Av and gives it its blessing, as Yehudah gives to Shimon.

title.en: From cow's horn to the shofar of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Av lacks the quality of Rosh Chodesh, and that in Matos-Masei the 'yerach ben yomo' of Nissan serves the 'karnei parah' of Av, turning it into the shofar of Moshiach. He adds that the 'migrash' around the Levite cities, from 'gerushin', alludes to exile, yet it remains joined to the city.

title.en: Hashem's ever-fresh love and the vessels of Midian

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem's love for Klal Yisroel never fades but is fresh every day like 'ben yomo'. He asks why the vessels of Midian needed kashering even when not 'ben yomo', and answers that Bilaam, Moav and Midian tried to spoil this love, so measure for measure their impurity is always fresh.

title.en: Yaakov's gift to Esav and the gid hanasheh

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Tammuz and Av belong to Esav, and that the animals Yaakov sent Esav were Jewish souls, weak ones, that he was forced to place under Esav's rule. Yaakov's injured gid hanasheh, which sforim link to Tisha B'Av, stands for forgotten souls, yet like a mother who cannot forget her child, they must all return.

title.en: Dinah, Osnas and Moshiach ben Yosef

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the Midrash that from Dinah's captivity in Shechem was born Osnas, who was carried to Egypt, raised by Potiphar and became Yosef's wife and the mother of Moshiach ben Yosef. As a spark of Moshiach ben David lay in Moav, a great treasure lay in Shechem, and likewise in Tisha B'Av.

title.en: Exile to gather sparks

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets the seven haftaros of consolation against the seven 'pazers', and brings the Ramchal that Hashem's plan is carried out even through sins, and the Gemara that Hashem scattered Israel among the nations to gain converts. The forgotten souls of the gid hanasheh fell among the nations, and in the days of Moshiach Esav will have to return the 'minchah'.

title.en: Why Dinah was taken: Hashem's plan

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ohr HaChaim that Hashem sometimes lets tzaddikim slip slightly so they will descend to raise holiness, and explains that Shechem ben Chamor held a holy spark of Moshiach ben Yosef. Through gematriaos and the Midrash that Dinah was first formed as Yosef, he shows Dinah was born to redeem that spark, and that she went out for the sake of Heaven.

title.en: Tisha B'Av on Shabbos heals the gid hanasheh

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Tisha B'Av is the day of the gid hanasheh in time as Shechem is in place, and brings the Edom stanza of 'Baruch Hashem yom yom' ending 'ki lo yiznach l'olam Hashem'. This year, when Pesach and Tisha B'Av fell on Shabbos, Shabbos heals the gid hanasheh as Yaakov arrived 'shalem' on Shabbos, and the days of Av hold great hidden treasures.

title.en: Exile as a mission; the seven weeks of consolation

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Shabbos Nachamu as the visit of a great guest, Yeshaya the prophet, for whom one must prepare. He stresses that exile is not merely punishment but a mission to gather the sparks, which is what 'ki mal'ah tzva'ah' means, and counts fifty days from the eleventh of Av to Rosh Hashanah, seven weeks of consolation.

title.en: Waiting with emunah; the greatness of exile revealed

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban that since all the prophecies of exile came true, its promised end will surely come too; one may not lose emunah, as Hashem asks His people to wait and Moshiach will not delay. He cites the Shomer Emunim's practice of a daily immersion for the holiness of Moshiach, and describes how, when Moshiach comes, the greatness of Israel in exile will be revealed even to the nations.

title.en: Tu B'Av: rising from the grave, the full moon

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells that in the desert people died every Tisha B'Av, and in the last year none died; on the fifteenth of Av, seeing the full moon, they knew the decree had ended and the day became a Yom Tov. Tisha B'Av is the diminished moon, and on the fifteenth of Av a Jew must rise from his 'grave' and serve Hashem.

title.en: Receiving the good tidings of Yeshaya

summary.en: The Mashgiach closes that on Shabbos Nachamu Yeshaya comes with good tidings for Yerushalayim. He brings the Me'or Einayim that one who announces good news, and one who receives it, gains a spark of Eliyahu HaNavi, an auspicious time for teshuvah, so one should receive the prophet's consolation and become an ehrlicher Yid.

catalogTitle: פרה אדומה - A מצוה that is Above our Understanding

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parah Adumah, the chok no one can understand, is the cure for the sin of Adam HaRishon, who wanted to understand beyond his reach, and that its lesson of faith and waiting prepares the Jewish people for Nisan and the Geulah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the halachos of Parah Adumah: since we have no red heifer, all are tamei, yet hearing Parshas Parah removes the inner tumah. He links Parah to Purim: Purim comforts those left outside the camp, while Parah purifies them and brings them in, preparing for Parshas HaChodesh and Nisan. On Rosh Chodesh Nisan the Satan argues that the Jews are unworthy of redemption; Parah, a chok done without reason, answers that Hashem may redeem without reason. He traces tumah to the Nachash, who is the Satan, and to Adam and Chava's desire for intellect beyond their reach, which brought death, the highest tumah, into the world. Doing a mitzvah without understanding is the tikkun. Two things are closed to the mind: how Parah works and when Moshiach will come. Judaism is built on waiting, since the first sin, the golden calf and Shaul's failure were all failures to wait, while Dovid waited.

en: Without a red heifer everyone today is tamei from contact with the dead, but hearing Parshas Parah removes the inner tumah that blocks a person from kedushah.
Parshas Parah completes Purim: Purim comforts those outside the camp, while Parah purifies them and lets them enter.
Parah, a chok kept without understanding, answers the Satan's claim on Rosh Chodesh Nisan that the Jews have no reason to be redeemed.
Death, brought by the sin of the Eitz HaDaas, is itself tumah, and Parah Adumah is the antidote to the venom of the Nachash.
The sin of Adam was wanting to understand beyond his reach, and doing a mitzvah without understanding is its tikkun.
Judaism is built on waiting, because the first sin was a failure to wait.

candidateTopics: Rosh Chodesh Nisan and the Geulah

title.en: Tumah today and the reading of Parah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the red heifer and explains that without it everyone today is tamei and cannot go up on Har HaBayis. He says that hearing Parshas Parah with faith removes the inner tumah, as a body has a neshamah, so tumah has an outer and an inner part.

title.en: Parah as the completion of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach ties Parah to Pur through the gematria and brings that Parshas Parah continues Purim, since Shabbos lifts up the week. Purim saves those expelled from the camp but leaves them outside; Parah purifies them and brings them in, so they enter Parshas HaChodesh renewed.

title.en: Nisan and the Satan's accusation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Nisan is the month of birth and redemption, and that on Rosh Chodesh Nisan kings are appointed in Heaven. The good malachim move that Hashem become King and Moshiach come, but the Satan argues the Jews are not worthy and the matter is put off.

title.en: A chok beyond understanding answers the Satan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parah is a chok that even Shlomo HaMelech could not understand, and that keeping it shows Klal Yisrael's deep emunah. Since Jews do a mitzvah without a reason, Hashem can redeem them without a reason. Parshas Parah is the deepest Shabbos of the year, the last one feeding the week of Adar.

title.en: The Nachash, the Satan and the lure of intellect

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks where the yetzer hara comes from and explains that Adam and Chava had no inner desires before the sin. The Nachash and the Satan are one, as their gematria shows; he could only tempt them with higher understanding, the knowledge of good and bad.

title.en: Death is tumah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that death, the punishment for the sin, is really tumah, which is why a corpse is the highest level of tumah. Life is the G-dliness in a person; the malach hamaves pulls it out and injects tumah, and Parah Adumah is the antidote to that venom.

title.en: A mitzvah without understanding as the tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tumas meis came because Adam and Chava wanted understanding beyond them, so its cure is a mitzvah done without understanding. Understanding is a fringe benefit, not a condition for keeping mitzvos; Parah brings life, as its mayim chaim and the passuk about the tzaddik living by his emunah show.

title.en: Two closed doors: Parah and the time of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach says we are in ikvesa d'meshicha and names two things the mind may not enter: how Parah works and when Moshiach will come. He brings Yaakov Avinu, Daniel and Achashverosh's miscalculation, and compares the Jews' disappointment then to the disappointment after the Holocaust.

title.en: Judaism is built on waiting

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew must wait, and contrasts a gentile served breakfast in bed with a Jew who must wash, daven and make hamotzi before eating. He brings the Ohr HaChaim that the Eitz HaDaas was a vine whose grapes Adam was meant to keep for Kiddush on Shabbos, so the first sin was not waiting.

title.en: The egel, Shaul and Dovid: waiting for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at Matan Torah death could have ended, but the golden calf came from not waiting for Moshe Rabbeinu. Shaul lost his kingdom for not waiting for Shmuel, while Dovid waited for the sound in the treetops, so Moshiach comes from him. He ends that waiting for Moshiach is waiting for the world to be sprinkled with Parah.
